title: Arrival — Narita to Akihabara

items.detail: LY91 lands 13:20 at Terminal 1. Allow 60–90 min for immigration and bags: you are out by 14:20–14:50. All Skyliner seats are reserved: buy yours at the Keisei ticket machine or counter in the Terminal 1 station, under the terminal. ⚑ Buy Nov 11's seat at the same time — the 11:05 from Nippori to Narita. Seats go on sale a month ahead, so you can buy it now and skip an errand on Nov 10. If the machine refuses your card, pay cash (the ATMs are on your way).

transit.label: Skyliner — Narita T1 → Nippori
transit.detail: Departures 14:38 · 14:59 · 15:18 · 15:37 · 15:59 — take the first one after you clear arrivals. 40 min to Nippori (the 15:18 makes two extra stops). You reach the hotel between 15:35 and 16:40. Last Skyliner 23:00. If Keisei is not running: JR N’EX to Tokyo Station.
transit.cost_note: station ticket, one way; some published fares say ¥2,470

transit.label: JR Yamanote or Keihin-Tōhoku — Nippori → Akihabara
transit.detail: At Nippori, follow the JR signs from the Keisei platform — allow 7 min. Take the first JR Yamanote or Keihin-Tōhoku train toward Ueno and Tokyo; both stop at Akihabara. 4 stops on the Yamanote.
transit.cost_note: with Suica; ¥200 with a paper ticket

transit.label: Walk — Akihabara Station to the hotel

items.detail: Check-in 14:00–22:00; 22:00 is a hard close. You arrive 15:35–16:40. You carry both bags the whole way (no luggage forwarding). Nothing else is planned tonight: rest.

notes_top: 💴 Get yen at an ATM in Terminal 1 before you leave the airport — they take foreign cards. Carry ¥30,000–40,000: about 40 temple and shrine gates on this trip take cash only.

items.label: What to buy
items.detail: Four things to buy: a camera, a fountain pen and stationery, a Seiko or Grand Seiko watch, and Uniqlo clothes. Choose the order and the areas on the day.

items.label: Where
items.detail: Shopping areas: Akihabara, Shibuya, Shinjuku and Ginza. Buy the watch and the Uniqlo clothes in Ginza: the Uniqlo flagship store is there, and the watch shops are listed in the watch section below. Buy the pen and stationery either in Ginza or at Sekaido in Shinjuku (next item).

items.label: Sekaido, Shinjuku — pens and stationery
items.detail: Art and stationery shop: Sekaido main store (世界堂 新宿本店), Shinjuku 3-1-1. 1 min from Shinjuku-sanchōme station exit C-4, 7 min from JR Shinjuku station. 🔴 Open 09:30–20:00 every day except the New Year holidays, so it works on either shopping day. 5 floors: 1F stationery, office supplies and fountain pens · 2F paper, drafting and design · 3F paints and art materials · 4F–5F framing. ⚑ Come for the discount. Stationery, art, design and comic supplies are 5–20% off the list price, and oil paints and painting media are 30% off. The point card gives back a further 7% of the discounted price. ⚠ Sekaido does not advertise tax-free shopping. Count on the discount only, and ask about tax-free at the register.

items.label: Tax-free is free today
items.detail: Until Oct 31, the shop takes the tax off at the register, and there is nothing to do at Narita. From Nov 1, Japan changes the system: you pay the tax in the shop and get it back only after customs confirms you took the goods out of Japan. Carry your passport. To qualify, spend ¥5,000 or more before tax, at one store on one day.

items.label: Bic Camera tourist coupon — 7% more on a Seiko
items.detail: Tap the coupon to open it full screen. At the till, before you pay, show it with your passport. The cashier scans both barcodes, ① and ②. Bic takes off the 10% tax, then another 7% off watches. The extra 7% applies to Seiko watches. It does not apply to Grand Seiko or to foreign-brand watches. Any payment method. Valid at every Bic Camera until Oct 31. If the till won't accept it: open the live coupon page with the button below.
items.image_alt: Bic Camera tourist coupon — barcodes ① and ②, valid to 2026-10-31

items.label: A Friday is the transaction day
items.detail: Buy today: on a weekday the tax-free desks have the shortest queues. Ginza and Akihabara close their main streets to cars on Sundays only, so you will see that on the second shopping day, Sunday Oct 25.

blocks.title: The watch — Seiko or Grand Seiko

items.label: Which shop for which watch
items.detail: Grand Seiko: buy at one of the two Ginza boutiques below. No shop gives more than the 10% tax off a Grand Seiko, and the boutiques have the widest range, including models sold only there. Seiko (Presage, Prospex and other lines): try it on at Seiko House, then buy at Bic Camera Yurakucho with the coupon, for the 10% tax plus 7% off. Bic is about 500 m from Seiko House on foot, or you can get there underground from Ginza station.

Seiko's store in the clock-tower building (Wako) at the Ginza 4-chome crossing, directly connected to Ginza station exit B1. Try on both brands here. 1F (Watch Square): Seiko and Grand Seiko. 2F: the Grand Seiko Flagship Boutique. Opens at 11:00. To buy: show your passport before you pay and say 免税でお願いします (menzei de onegai shimasu, “tax-free, please”).

Grand Seiko's largest shop in Japan. It sells only Grand Seiko, including the models sold only in its boutiques. On Namiki-dori, about 300 m west of Seiko House. To buy: show your passport before you pay and say 免税でお願いします (menzei de onegai shimasu, “tax-free, please”).

Electronics store, 1 min from JR Yūrakuchō station (Hibiya exit). Buy a Seiko here, with the coupon. Watches are on 6F. At the till, before you pay, show the coupon (at the top of this day) and your passport.

Electronics store 1 min from the hotel, open until 22:00. Use it to try on watches any evening, or to buy if you don't get to Ginza. Watches are on 3F, the same floor as the cameras. Tax-free with your passport. The Bic Camera 7% coupon does not work here.

transit.label: In-town hops — Ginza / Shinjuku / Akihabara
transit.detail: Trains and subways run by different companies. Suica works on all of them.
transit.cost_note: rough estimate for the day

backup.title: Not a weather day — but if the day is given up for something else
backup.detail: Everything on this day is indoors, so rain changes nothing. If you give up the day for another reason, replace it with a trip in the Tokyo area that needs no change of trains. The best fit is Yokohama and Sankei-en.

transit.label: JR Yamanote or Keihin-Tōhoku — Akihabara → Ueno
transit.detail: Take the first JR Yamanote or Keihin-Tōhoku train toward Ueno; both stop there. 2 stops on the Yamanote. At Ueno, leave by the Park Exit (公園口), which opens onto Ueno Park and its museums. The Tokyo National Museum is about 10 min on foot from the exit.
transit.cost_note: with Suica; ¥160 with a paper ticket

items.detail: Spend the morning in the Honkan and the Heiseikan. Your ¥2,100 Daitoku-ji exhibition ticket also gets you into the standing collection on the day you use it, so you pay nothing more at the gate. Walk straight past the main-gate ticket window: its queue can take over 30 min at busy times. Saturday hours run to 20:00, last admission 19:30. Today's plan is full: if you are running late, skim the standing collection, which you saw in 2019.
items.about: The museum counts about 120,000 objects in its collection, 89 of them National Treasures and 648 Important Cultural Properties. The Honkan holds the Japanese art galleries; the Heiseikan holds the archaeology halls.

items.detail: About 10 min on foot across Ueno Park. Allow about 1½ hours for the permanent collection. Eat lunch before or after this museum, in Ueno or on the walk down into Yanaka.
items.about: The main building was designed by Le Corbusier, and the building itself is the UNESCO World Heritage site, so the architecture is half the reason to come.

items.detail: 15–20 min on foot downhill from Ueno Park. The afternoon is a walk through Yanaka (谷中) to Nezu-jinja. Allow 1½–2 hours, and make it longer or shorter to fit the day. If you are running late, skip Yanaka Ginza and the cemetery and go straight to Nezu-jinja.
items.about: A short shopping street of about sixty small shops. The low-rise streets around it look like the old Tokyo that has disappeared from most of the city.

items.detail: Walk through it on the way west: first the temple lanes, then the cemetery's central avenue. The paths are public and there is no gate.
items.about: A Tokyo city cemetery, opened in 1874. Cherry trees line its central avenue.

items.detail: The last stop of the walk. Allow 30–45 min. ⚠ Arrive by about 17:00: the Karamon gate closes at 17:30 in October.
items.about: The shrine's halls were built in 1706 and survive intact; they are an Important Cultural Property. Look for the Otome-Inari tunnel of red torii gates and the pond garden.

transit.label: Chiyoda line + JR — Nezu → Akihabara, changing at Ochanomizu
transit.detail: About 20 min from the shrine, two trains. From Nezu station, take the Chiyoda line to Shin-Ochanomizu. Walk 3 min across to JR Ochanomizu. Take the Chūō-Sōbu line 1 stop to Akihabara. The Chiyoda line does not go to Akihabara.
transit.cost_note: with Suica, both trains together

backup.title: If it rains — the hill absorbs it, and the day barely moves
backup.detail: Most of this day is indoors: the Tokyo National Museum in the morning and the Museum of Western Art in the early afternoon. Only the walk down into Yanaka is outdoors. In steady rain, replace that walk with another museum in Ueno Park. Don't swap this day with another date. Sunday has free time set aside for anything you don't finish today, so the two days must stay next to each other.

items.label: The day has two jobs
items.detail: Finish any shopping left over from Friday (Day 2). Use the rest of the day for anything from Saturday's Ueno day (Day 3) that you didn't get to before dark.

items.label: Sunday is the only day the streets close
items.detail: On Sundays from October to March, the main shopping streets in Ginza and Akihabara are closed to traffic: Ginza's Chūō-dōri 12:00–17:00, Akihabara 13:00–17:00. Today is the trip's only chance to walk them car-free.

items.label: Tax-free, still the old way
items.detail: Tax-free shopping still works the old way today: the tax comes off at the register, and there is nothing to show customs on your departure morning. The rules change on Nov 1.

items.label: The watch carries over
items.detail: If you didn't buy the watch on Friday, the watch plan on Day 2 still applies today. The Bic Camera coupon is valid until Oct 31. Sunday hours: Seiko House 11:00–19:00, Grand Seiko Namiki boutique 11:00–19:00, Bic Camera Yurakucho 10:00–22:00.

items.label: Sekaido is open today too
items.detail: Sekaido Shinjuku main store (世界堂 新宿本店), the stationery stop from Day 2, is open 09:30–20:00 every day of the year. ⚑ The car-free streets end at 17:00 and Sekaido stays open until 20:00, so go to Shinjuku after Ginza and Akihabara. Full details on Day 2.

transit.label: Akihabara ⇄ Ginza ×2 — Tokyo Metro
transit.cost_note: rough estimate for the day

backup.title: If Monday or Tuesday looks rainy, swap it with today
backup.detail: Everything today is indoors, the shops are open every day of the week, and none of it needs daylight, so today can swap with either outdoor Tokyo day. If the forecast shows heavy rain all day for Monday (Mount Takao, Day 5) or Tuesday (Kamakura, Day 6), do that day today and go shopping on the wet day. Decide this morning: once today has passed, the swap is no longer possible. What you give up: the car-free streets in Ginza and Akihabara (Sundays only), and the time set aside for anything left over from Saturday's Ueno day. By this morning you will know whether you need that time.

title: Mount Takao

items.label: Buy lunch at the konbini
items.detail: Buy onigiri or sandwiches at a konbini in Akihabara before you board the train, and eat them on the summit deck. You can't count on any place to eat on the mountain. The two teahouses at the summit, the two you pass on Trail 1 and the old soba house at the foot of the mountain all close on irregular days, and none of them publishes a calendar. If that soba house is open on your way down, it serves hot tororo soba (soba with grated yam) until last order at 16:30 on weekdays. There is time for it on the descent, but eating there means skipping the tsukemen dinner in Shinjuku, where you need to arrive by 16:30.

transit.label: JR + Keiō — Akihabara → Takaosanguchi
transit.detail: Leave the hotel at about 08:30. Take JR to Shinjuku, then the Keiō Takao line to Takaosanguchi, the last stop. About 1½ hours in all; the Keiō part alone is about an hour. ⚠ A map app may suggest an all-JR route to Takao first. Ignore it: it costs ¥1,174 instead of ¥639. Takaosanguchi is the trailhead. Trail 1 starts a few minutes' walk from the ticket gate.
transit.cost_note: one way; ¥1,278 round trip

maps.label: Trail map — Tokyo's Takao Visitor Centre
maps.note: All six numbered trails plus Inariyama. Same office that posts trail closures.

maps.label: AllTrails — Trail 6, the way down
maps.note: Covers the descent only. ⚠ AllTrails has no Trail 1 route of its own — its Takao entries are Trails 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, Inariyama, and a combined Inariyama + Trail 1 — so our ascent is not mapped there as we walk it. ⚠ Ignore the orange "Takao Partial Closure" alert on that page — it is dated October 2025 and says Trail 6 is shut to downhill walkers. Tokyo's own visitor centre lifted that on 8 May 2026: "Trail 6 can now be used for descent as well." The visitor centre link above is the live source.

transit.label: On foot — Takaosanguchi → Yakuō-in (Trail 1 · 1号路)
transit.detail: A paved path with an even slope up through cedar forest and the Jōshinmon gate (浄心門). Allow 1–1¼ hours at an easy pace. The cable car runs alongside if you need it, but the walk up is the point of the day. ⚑ Phone maps label the trails in Japanese only. Look for 1号路 (Trail 1), written in full as 自然研究路1号路. It is also signed 表参道 (the temple approach). Past the Jōshinmon gate the path splits into 男坂 (Otokozaka, a staircase of 108 steps) and 女坂 (Onnazaka, a gentler curving path). They join again, so take either.

items.detail: Temple about two-thirds of the way up Trail 1. Allow 30–45 min. Free to enter. It stands on the open mountain and has no gate hours. ⏱ Be past the temple by 14:50, and leave the summit by 15:25. From here it is 30 min to the summit and up to 1½ hours down Trail 6, so that gets you down by sunset (16:55; last light 17:21). If you reach the temple after 14:50: skip the summit and walk back down Trail 1 to the cable car (last car down 18:00). If you are still at the summit after 15:25: go back down Trail 1 to the cable car instead of taking Trail 6.
items.about: A working Shingon Buddhist temple on the mountain. Look for the Niōmon gate, the main hall, the Gongen-dō and the okunoin (inner sanctuary), and the statues of tengu (long-nosed mountain goblins) Mt Takao is known for.

transit.label: On foot — Yakuō-in → the 599 m summit
transit.detail: 30 min more on the upper part of Trail 1.

items.detail: Allow about 30 min at the viewing deck, plus lunch there: roughly 12:30–13:30.
items.about: The summit of Mt Takao is 599 m high. The viewing deck looks out over the Kantō plain and, on a clear day, to Mt Fuji.

transit.label: On foot — the summit → Takaosanguchi (Trail 6 · 6号路)
transit.detail: An unpaved path down the Biwa-taki valley, beside a stream. Of the two unpaved trails down, this is the gentler one. Allow 1¼–1½ hours. If your legs are tired at the summit: walk down Trail 1 instead, and take the cable car (until 18:00) or the chairlift (until about 16:30) from its top station. ⚑ On a phone map look for 6号路 (Trail 6) or 自然研究路6号路. The visitor centre also signs it 琵琶滝コース (Biwa-taki course), after the waterfall it passes. ⚠ Do not take 稲荷山コース (Inariyama course) or 3号路 (Trail 3) by mistake. Both are signposted at the summit, and neither is this route.

transit.label: Keiō + JR — Takaosanguchi → Akihabara
transit.detail: The Keiō line back to Shinjuku, then JR on to Akihabara.
transit.cost_note: one way; ¥1,278 round trip

notes_top: 💴 Bring cash. The teahouses and stalls on the mountain are cash only. One listing says the highest teahouse at the summit takes JCB and AMEX cards, but don't rely on it. The first-choice dinner, Gonokami Seisakusho in Shinjuku, is cash only too. Both backup dinners take cards.

backup.title: If it rains — the day moves, and if it cannot move it shrinks
backup.detail: Rain takes away what this day is for: the walk up and the view from the summit. First choice: swap it with Tuesday's Kamakura day. That is the only day left that can swap with this one. If you can't swap, do a shorter version. Take the cable car up to Yakuō-in, then visit the TAKAO 599 MUSEUM by Takaosanguchi station (free, 8:00–17:00, last entry 16:30). You keep the temple but lose the mountain walk.

title: Kita-Kamakura Zen

transit.label: JR — Akihabara → Kita-Kamakura, changing at Tokyo
transit.detail: Two trains, one JR fare: tap in at Akihabara, tap out at Kita-Kamakura. Akihabara → Tokyo: Yamanote or Keihin-Tōhoku line, 2 stops. Tokyo → Kita-Kamakura: Yokosuka line. About 70 min in all. Faster (under an hour, same fare): from Tokyo take any train to Ōfuna, then change to the Yokosuka line for the next stop, Kita-Kamakura.
transit.cost_note: one way; ¥2,068 round trip

items.detail: 1 min from the platform. Allow about an hour. 💴 Cash only.
items.about: A hillside compound of about thirty sub-temples climbing the valley: the great Sanmon gate, the Butsuden hall, and — up its own flight of steps — the Ōgane, a National Treasure bell cast in 1301, visible any day.

items.detail: 7–10 min along the lane. Allow 30–45 min for the main grounds and the round window. The rear garden is closed on this date (it opens only in June and late November).
items.about: The temple of the round window, Satori-no-mado. The rear garden opens for the June hydrangeas and the late-November maples.

items.detail: 15–20 min further down the same street. Allow 1–1½ hours. 💴 Cash only. Carry a snack: lunch is late, at Kamakura Station after Hachimangū.
items.about: Head temple of the Kamakura Five Mountains, founded in 1253: the Sanmon gate, the Butsuden, the Hōjō and the Kara-mon gate. Beside the Sanmon hangs a second National Treasure bell, cast in 1255.

items.label: Optional — the Hansōbō climb to the Shōjōken viewpoint
items.detail: From the back of the precinct: about 250 steps up to Hansōbō, then about 180 more to the Shōjōken viewpoint. 45 min–1 hour there and back: return the same way, not onto the Ten'en ridge trail. ⏱ Start before 15:00. In rain the steps are slippery: skip it.
items.about: Hansōbō is Kenchō-ji's hilltop guardian shrine, lined with tengu statues. From Shōjōken you look over Sagami Bay and, on a clear day, to Fuji.

items.detail: 15 min downhill from Kenchō-ji. Allow 30–45 min for the main approach and the hall.
items.about: Kamakura's central shrine. Minamoto no Yoritomo moved it to this site in 1180, the same year he set up the first samurai government in Kamakura. Wakamiya Ōji, the 2 km avenue from the beach, was built in 1182.

transit.label: Walk — Tsurugaoka Hachimangū → Kamakura Station
transit.detail: 10 min downhill to the station's east exit. Lunch is at Kawashige, 3 min from the exit.

transit.label: JR Yokosuka line — Kamakura → Akihabara
transit.detail: About 65 min, two trains. Yokosuka line to Tokyo, then Yamanote or Keihin-Tōhoku line 2 stops to Akihabara.
transit.cost_note: one way; ¥2,068 round trip

notes_top: 💴 A cash day: Engaku-ji, Meigetsu-in, Kenchō-ji and the late lunch all take cash only. Draw enough before you leave Tokyo.
notes: 💴 Tonight, pay the Akihabara hotel bill at the front desk: ¥175,695 for six nights plus ¥1,200 lodging tax. Tomorrow's 09:30 train leaves no time in the morning.

backup.title: If it rains — the temples hold, the climb goes
backup.detail: The temples stay open in rain; skip only the Hansōbō climb. Use the freed hour at Tōkei-ji: 4 min from Kita-Kamakura station on the same street, free, 9:00–16:00, and its treasure house is open on this date.

title: Travel — Tokyo to Kyoto

items.detail: Breakfast buffet on the 3rd floor, included, from 06:30: eat 06:30–07:15. Nothing was prepaid. At the front desk you pay ¥175,695 for the six nights plus ¥1,200 lodging tax. If you didn't pay last night, be at the desk by 08:10. Leave at 08:25.

transit.label: JR Yamanote or Keihin-Tōhoku — Akihabara → Tokyo
transit.detail: 2 stops via Kanda, 5 min. Take the first Yamanote or Keihin-Tōhoku train. It is the weekday rush and you have a trolley, so you may have to let a full train go. Timing: leave the hotel at 08:25 · 5 min to walk the 150 m, pass the Akihabara gate and reach the platform · up to 5 min waiting for a train · 5 min on the train. You get off at Tokyo at about 08:40 and reach the ekiben (boxed lunch) shop at about 08:45. You stay inside the ordinary JR gates the whole way, so you can buy lunch before the Shinkansen gate.
transit.cost_note: with Suica; ¥160 with a paper ticket

blocks.title: Ekiben (boxed lunch): buy it before the Shinkansen gate

items.detail: Ekibenya Matsuri, an ekiben (boxed lunch) shop on the 1st floor of GRANSTA, on the central passage inside the ordinary JR gates. Buy your box between 08:45 and 09:00. At 09:00, stop shopping and walk to the Shinkansen gate, even if you haven't chosen. 🔴 Buy before you pass the Tōkaidō Shinkansen transfer gate: once you are through, you cannot come back. About 150 kinds, changing with the deliveries and the time of day. Open from 05:30 every day. Pay with Suica or a credit card (JRE POINT also works); you don't need cash. Go through the transfer gate by about 09:05: tap the Wallet Suica registered to smartEX. There is no ticket to collect. Then go up to the platform shown on the departure board, about 10 min from the shop. You are on the platform at about 09:15. Your car number is on the smartEX booking, and markings on the platform floor show where each car stops. Eat your box on the train, at about 11:00–11:35.

transit.label: Nozomi — Tokyo 09:30 → Kyoto 11:44
transit.detail: Reserved seat on the 09:30 Nozomi to Hakata, arriving at Kyoto at 11:44. If you miss it, later trains leave at 09:39, 09:45, 09:48, 09:54 and 10:00. The 09:39 reaches Kyoto at 11:50, only 6 minutes after the 09:30.
transit.cost_note: smartEX flexible fare, reserved seat, no early-booking discount; ¥14,170 for the same seat at a station counter

transit.label: Walk — Kyoto Station to the Dormy Inn
transit.detail: 3 min from the Central (Karasuma) gate, on the north side of the station.

items.detail: At about 11:55, ask the front desk to hold both bags until check-in (normally free). If the desk can't take them: coin lockers at Kyoto Station, 3 min back. That costs 20–30 min and a locker fee. Check-in is 15:00. At this desk you pay ¥274,000 for the ten nights, in full and in yen, plus the Kyoto lodging tax of about ¥10,000. The desk works out the exact tax.

items.label: Free afternoon in Kyoto
items.detail: One errand: buy the Nov 7 and Nov 9 Shinkansen tickets at Kyoto Station (see the ticket note at the end of today). Nothing else is planned this afternoon. Spend it on foot, starting from the station, however you feel when you arrive.

notes_top: 💳 Today's train is booked on smartEX: go through the Shinkansen gate by tapping the registered IC card or scanning the smartEX QR code. Don't collect a paper ticket from a machine. The Nov 7 and Nov 9 trains are different: you buy paper tickets for them at Kyoto Station this afternoon (see the note at the end of today).

💴 Budget ¥15,000–18,000 in cash for the ten Kyoto nights, on top of temple and shrine entry fees. Several dinners are cash-only, and some of their backups are too: on Nov 2 and Nov 6, neither the first choice nor the backup takes cards or IC. Top up your cash as you go instead of drawing it all at once.
notes: 🎫 Before you leave Kyoto Station this afternoon, buy the Shinkansen tickets for Nov 7 and Nov 9. Use a reserved-seat ticket machine (指定席券売機) by the Shinkansen gates and press English. Sat Nov 7: Nozomi 13, Kyoto 10:02 → Hiroshima, any reserved seat, ¥11,940. Mon Nov 9: Nozomi 26, Hiroshima 12:43 → Tokyo, seat E (the Fuji side), ¥19,760. 🔴 If you pay by credit card, the machine asks for the card's PIN. Know your PIN, or pay in cash, or buy from a person at the JR ticket office (みどりの窓口, Midori-no-madoguchi). On each travel day, put all of that day's tickets into the gate together, and take them back on the other side. If plans change: one free change of train or date at a ticket office before departure. If you miss the train: the same tickets are valid in the non-reserved cars of a later train that day.

✈ Tonight, check two web pages for Monday Nov 9's dinner in Tokyo. It is the only evening on the trip where neither the first choice nor the backup publishes its November opening days before late October. First, Kamayoshi's own X feed for its November opening days. It posts them month by month, and they can differ from its usual closing on Sundays and holidays. Second, Atre Akihabara's November calendar, for the backup. If Kamayoshi hasn't posted November yet, check again on Nov 7.

title: Ikaruga & Nishinokyō

transit.label: JR — Kyoto → Hōryūji
transit.detail: Leave the hotel at 07:45 for the 08:02 train. You arrive at Hōryūji at 09:26. Take the JR Nara line to Nara, then the Yamatoji line west: Hōryūji is 11 min past Nara. From the station the temple is about 20 min on foot, north. Or take the bus signed Hōryūji-sandō, a short ride.

items.detail: Go here first: Yakushi-ji and Tōshōdai-ji, later today, stop letting visitors in at 16:30. Allow 1½–2 hours. See the Western Precinct, the Daihōzōin treasure galleries, and the Yumedono hall in the Eastern Precinct. One ¥2,000 ticket covers all three. 💴 Cash only. ⚑ The Guze Kannon statue in the Yumedono is on show today. It is shown only from 22 October to 22 November each year. Today the temple closes at 17:00 and last entry is 16:30. From 4 November it closes at 16:30 and last entry is 16:00.
items.about: The Western Precinct holds the kondō (main hall) and the five-storey pagoda, the oldest surviving wooden buildings in the world. The Daihōzōin galleries hold the temple's treasures. The Yumedono is an octagonal hall in the Eastern Precinct.

transit.label: Walk — Hōryū-ji to Hōryūji Station
transit.detail: Eat lunch on this walk. Nishinokyō, the next stop, has nowhere to eat. The first-choice lunch, Fukokuen, is 3–4 min south-east of the Yumedono. The two backups, Hiraso and Matsumotoya, are 400 m west, on the street that leads to the temple gate. From any of the three, the walk south to the station takes the same 20 min. If a Hōryūji-sandō bus is at the stop, it takes 5 min.

transit.label: JR then Kintetsu — Hōryūji → Nishinokyō, changing at Kōriyama
transit.detail: Take JR 2 stops east to Kōriyama, 7 min. Then walk 15 min across the town centre to Kintetsu-Kōriyama station. The two stations are on opposite sides of town, in separate buildings. Take Kintetsu 2 stops north to Nishinokyō, 1 min from Yakushi-ji. Both lines run about 4 trains an hour and take your IC card at the normal gates. The longest you will wait for a train is about 15 min. ⚑ A possible shortcut: Nara Kōtsū bus #97, a loop route, runs hourly from the Hōryūji-mae stop at the temple gate straight to Yakushi-ji in 45 min, with no walking. It runs only in some seasons and the operator does not publish the dates, so plan on the trains. If the bus is running: get on by the rear door and tap your card. Get off by the front door and tap again at the reader beside the driver. You tap twice because the fare depends on the distance.
transit.cost_note: ¥200 JR + ¥180 Kintetsu, paid separately; there is no through ticket

items.detail: 1 min from Nishinokyō Station. Allow about 1½ hours. Last entry 16:30; the gate closes at 17:00.
items.about: The East Pagoda is the only building left from the temple's founding. The West Pagoda, the kondō (main hall) and the Great Lecture Hall are 20th-century reconstructions, built to the original Hakuhō-period plan.

items.detail: 10 min north on the same lane. Allow 1–1¼ hours. The ¥1,000 ticket covers the grounds; the treasure house costs ¥200 more. Last entry 16:30.
items.about: Founded by Ganjin, a Chinese monk who reached Japan on his sixth attempt. See the kondō (main hall) and its statues, and the grounds of Ganjin's mausoleum behind it.

transit.label: Walk — Tōshōdai-ji to Nishinokyō Station
transit.detail: Back down the lane the way you came, past Yakushi-ji’s south gate.

transit.label: Kintetsu — Nishinokyō → Kyoto
transit.detail: Take the Kashihara line north and change at Yamato-Saidaiji for the Kyoto line. Limited-express and express trains stop at Nishinokyō only from 10:00 to 16:59. If you leave later, take a local train to Yamato-Saidaiji and change there.
transit.cost_note: one way

notes: 🎫 Tonight at Kyoto Station, buy the ticket for tomorrow's 07:05 limited express to Kashihara: a ¥520 seat ticket, from the Kintetsu counter or machine. Tomorrow you leave at 06:45.

✈ Tonight, check Kaidashimen Kitada's Instagram for closing days. This ramen shop is the plan for four dinners: first choice on Oct 30 and Nov 5, backup tonight and on Nov 3. It closes on irregular days and publishes no schedule. A check made before the trip tells you nothing about this week.

backup.title: If another Kansai day looks rainy, swap it with today
backup.detail: Everything today is in large indoor halls: Hōryū-ji's precincts and treasure galleries, then Yakushi-ji and Tōshōdai-ji. It is the only Kansai day that works in all-day rain, so it has no rain version of its own. ⚑ If tomorrow's forecast is rain, decide this morning whether to swap: do tomorrow's plan today and today's plan tomorrow. From Oct 30, the only days left to swap a rainy day with are Nov 2 and Nov 6. If today runs long or the trains are disrupted, drop Tōshōdai-ji. It is the last stop and the smallest loss. The #97 bus not running does not count as a disruption: the trains take only about 6 min longer.

title: Yamanobe-no-michi — the old road

transit.label: Kintetsu 07:05 — Kyoto → Tenri 07:56, changing at Yamato-Saidaiji
transit.detail: Leave the hotel at 06:45. The Kintetsu ticket gates are on the south side of Kyoto Station, about 10 min away. The hotel breakfast opens at 06:30, too late to sit down to: buy breakfast at a konbini on the way and eat it on the train. Take the 07:05 limited express to Kashihara and get off at Yamato-Saidaiji at 07:34. From the same station, take the 07:39 express to Tenri, arriving 07:56. That gets you to Isonokami Jingū at about 08:30. The 07:05 needs a ¥520 reserved-seat ticket: buy it the night before, or at the Kintetsu counter or ticket machine before you board. Cheaper (¥910, no seat ticket): the 06:49 semi-express. Change at Ōkubo, then at Yamato-Saidaiji onto the same 07:39, arriving at the same 07:56. To catch it, leave the hotel by about 06:35. If you miss both: the 07:16 express goes to Tenri with no change, but arrives at 08:23. That leaves you 27 min less daylight at the end of the walk, at Ōmiwa. At Tenri, JR and Kintetsu share one station building, and the walk starts from it.
transit.cost_note: ¥910 fare + ¥520 reserved seat on the 07:05; ¥910 on the 06:49, which needs no seat ticket

blocks.title: Walk in through the town — 山の辺の道

maps.label: Course map — Nara Prefecture
maps.note: Printable sheets for the whole Tenri–Sakurai road, drawn on government survey maps.

maps.label: AllTrails — Yamanobe-no-michi
maps.note: Same road, mapped in the opposite direction — Sakurai to Tenri. We walk it north to south.

transit.label: Walk — Tenri Station to Isonokami Jingū
transit.detail: 2.5 km east: straight up the Tenri Hondōri shopping arcade, then over the Furu river. 40 min. There are konbini and supermarkets at the station end if you want food or drink for the walk.

items.detail: Allow 30–45 min. There are no tickets and nothing to go inside. The gates open at about 05:30 (the time shifts with the season), so 08:30 is well within the hours. The Yamanobe-no-michi walking road starts from behind the shrine.
items.about: The northern end of the Yamanobe-no-michi. The shrine held the weapons of the Yamato court, Japan's early ruling house. The haiden (worship hall) is a National Treasure. So is the haiden of the Izumo-Takeo shrine, a smaller shrine in the grounds that was moved here from elsewhere. The rōmon (two-storey gate) is an Important Cultural Property. Long-tailed roosters wander the cedar-lined approach.

blocks.title: The road south — to the Yanagimoto midpoint — 山の辺の道

transit.label: Walk — Isonokami Jingū to Chōgaku-ji
transit.detail: About 6.3 km, 2 hours 5 min of walking, on a farm track along the hillside. This is the longest walk of the trip, and the easiest ground of any walking day: about 75 m between the lowest and highest points, graded 2 out of 5 by Nara Prefecture. A station on the train line is never more than about 20 min away if you want to stop. On the way you pass orchards, stone-walled lanes, roadside vegetable stalls where you pay into an honesty box, and the burial mound of Emperor Sujin, which you see from its torii gate across the rice fields.

blocks.title: Chōgaku-ji, and lunch at the midpoint

items.detail: Allow 35–50 min. ⚑ From 23 October to the end of November the original hell screen (shown only from 23 October to the end of November) hangs in the main hall, so it is on show today. The head priest talks visitors through it at 13:00 on Saturdays and Sundays. Today is a Friday: a talk happens only if a group has booked one, and you may sit in if one is on. Lunch is a few minutes further on, at the Tenri City Trail Center (open 08:30–17:00). Its restaurant serves 11:00–16:30, Tuesday to Sunday, and is open today. ⏱ Leave the Trail Center by 14:30. The rest of the walk to Ōmiwa takes up to 1 hour 40 min, plus about 35 min of stops, so you arrive by about 16:45, before sunset (17:06). If you can't leave by 14:30, end the walk here: Yanagimoto station is 20 min (about 1 km) west, downhill off the walking road, on the JR Man'yō Mahoroba line home.
items.about: A temple at the midpoint of the Yamanobe-no-michi, founded in the 9th century. The bell-tower gate, from the Heian period, and the Amida triad in the main hall are both Important Cultural Properties. Beside them is a garden with a 400-year-old pine. The hell screen, 11 m by 4 m, was painted by Kanō Sanraku. A copy hangs in its place the rest of the year.

blocks.title: The road south — on to Hibara — 山の辺の道

transit.label: Walk — Chōgaku-ji to Hibara Shrine
transit.detail: The southern half of the road runs about 5 km from Yanagimoto to Ōmiwa, past Emperor Keikō's tomb and over a track along the ridge. Hibara Shrine is the first stop on it. Tenri City gives 1 hour 10 min of walking for the whole stretch to Ōmiwa. Its times for the northern half are slower than that, and at that slower pace this stretch takes nearer 1 hour 40 min.

blocks.title: Hibara Shrine, and the stops on the ridge

items.detail: An open-air shrine on the road, about 40 min north of Ōmiwa Jinja. There are no buildings and nothing that closes, so you can visit at any hour.
items.about: Known as Moto-Ise: the deity now worshipped at Ise is said to have been enshrined here before Ise itself. There is no hall and no honden (main sanctuary). A torii gate stands in the open and frames Mount Miwa, which is itself the object of worship.

items.label: Open-air stops between Hibara Shrine and Ōmiwa
items.detail: Five or six stops, all free, with no tickets and no queues: 20–35 min in total. They include Genpin-an, the Ōmiwa-no-Mori lookout over the whole Yamato basin and its three hills, and Sai Shrine on the way down.

transit.label: Walk — Hibara Shrine to Ōmiwa Jinja
transit.detail: The last part of the road, downhill off the hillside into the Ōmiwa Jinja grounds.

items.detail: Allow 45 min–1 hour. The shrine has no gate hours, so arriving late cannot shut you out. The walk runs north to south so that it ends here, where nothing closes. ⚠ Daylight: sunset today is 17:06, and last light (civil dusk) is 17:32. At the walking times given for today, you reach the end with about 30–40 min of daylight to spare. At the slower pace for the southern half, almost none is left. If the day has run late, end the walk early: there are five stations on the line, and you are never more than about 20 min from one. If you are still at the Trail Center after 14:30, end the walk at Yanagimoto station instead.
items.about: The southern end of the Yamanobe-no-michi, and the oldest form of Shinto still practised. There is no honden (main sanctuary), because Mount Miwa behind the shrine is itself the deity. Look for the great torii gate on the approach, the haiden (worship hall) and the cedar tree beside the hall.

transit.label: Walk — Ōmiwa Jinja to JR Miwa
transit.detail: 5 min from the great torii gate.

transit.label: JR and Kintetsu — Miwa → Kyoto
transit.detail: About 1½ hours. Take the JR Man’yō Mahoroba line out of Miwa, then Kintetsu or JR into Kyoto. You can go north through Nara or south through Sakurai: take whichever train the departure board at Miwa shows first. Trains run about twice an hour in the afternoon and about once an hour after 21:00. ⚠ The last train that gets you to Kyoto tonight leaves Miwa at 22:20 and arrives at 23:44. Later trains leave Miwa but stop short of Kyoto, and you would be stuck until morning.
transit.cost_note: up to ¥1,170, depending on the route

notes_top: 💴 Bring cash. The roadside stalls (you pay into an honesty box) and the small shrines along the road take nothing else.
notes: 🎫 Tonight, at the Kintetsu counter or machine as you come back through Kyoto Station, buy the ¥520 limited-express seat ticket for tomorrow’s 08:30 to Kintetsu Nara.

🌐 Tonight, check two websites for Sunday Nov 1: Kurama-dera's front page, which posts dated path closures, and Kifune Shrine's news page, which posts one-day changes to its hours. Sunday's whole day is the walk over the ridge between the two, and anything you checked before the trip will be two weeks old by then.

backup.title: If it rains: swap the whole day
backup.detail: This day is a walk along a hillside farm track, and there is no indoor version of it. If it rains, swap the whole day with another instead of trying to save part of it. The days you can still swap with are Monday Nov 2 (the Kamo shrines) and Friday Nov 6 (Uji). Thursday's Ikaruga day has already passed, so those two are the only ones. Nothing on this day is tied to its date, so the swap costs nothing.

transit.label: Kintetsu 08:30 limited express — Kyoto → Kintetsu Nara 09:04
transit.detail: Leave the hotel at 08:00. The Kintetsu gates are on the south side of Kyoto Station, about 10 min on foot; this train leaves from platform 2. Direct, 34 min. 🔴 Every seat is reserved. Buy the ¥520 seat ticket last night, or this morning at the Kintetsu counter or machine before you board. Pay the ¥760 fare with your IC card at the gate. If you miss it: the 08:55 limited express arrives about 09:30, or the 08:56 express (no seat ticket needed) arrives 09:42. Use Kintetsu both ways today. JR is too slow this morning: on Saturdays its first Miyakoji rapid leaves only at 09:04, and the local trains before it take over an hour. Kintetsu Nara is also nearer the park than JR Nara.
transit.cost_note: one way: ¥760 fare on the IC card + ¥520 reserved-seat ticket

transit.label: Bus — Kintetsu Nara → Tōdai-ji
transit.detail: City loop bus #2 from the stop outside the station, about 10 min. Get off at Tōdaiji Daibutsuden-mae. Walking takes about 20 min east through the park. The bus gives you more time in the Great Buddha Hall before your museum entry.
transit.payment: ⚠ Nara buses work the opposite way to Kyoto buses. Board by the front door and tap your IC card once as you get on. Get off by the rear door with nothing to do: the fare is flat, so you have already paid. If your card balance is short, pay cash into the box by the driver.
transit.cost_note: flat fare; your only bus today, since you walk back to Kintetsu Nara this evening

items.detail: Off the bus at about 09:20. Allow 45 min for the Nandaimon gate and the Great Buddha Hall. ⏱ Leave by 10:10: the museum is 15 min west through the park, and your entry window opens at 10:30. If you came on the 08:55 backup train: allow 30 min here. If you came later: go straight to the museum and see the hall after lunch. 💴 There is no combined ticket. The Hokke-dō, the Kaidan-dō and the Tōdai-ji Museum each charge their own admission, all cash only.
items.about: You enter through the Nandaimon gate, guarded by two Kamakura-period statues. The Great Buddha Hall is one of the largest wooden buildings in the world, rebuilt in 1709 after the hall burned twice. Inside sits the 14.98 m Rushana Buddha, cast in 749. In front of the hall stands an octagonal bronze lantern from the Nara period.

items.detail: 🔴 Your ticket is for Saturday 31 October, entry 10:30–11:00. The QR code is in Documents on the Info tab. It lets you in once, inside that window only. Arrive a few minutes after 10:30, to miss the crowd of ticket holders who all arrive at 10:30 exactly. No time limit once inside. Allow 1½–2 hours: the exhibition is small and crowded, and in 2025 two hours was not enough for visitors reading the labels. ⚠ The Buddhist sculpture hall is closed for renovation from 14 September 2026, so your ticket does not include it. The small Bronze Ware Hall next to it is free during the exhibition. Its upper floor shows some of the museum's statues, for a quiet 10 min before lunch.
items.about: The Shōsō-in is Tōdai-ji's imperial storehouse, and its treasures are shown once a year. This is the 78th exhibition: 60 treasures, 11 of them never shown before, in the East and West wings.

items.detail: After lunch, walk back east through the park, about 25 min from the arcade, past the Great Buddha Hall. Then walk 15 min up the hillside behind it. No gate and no ticket. Allow 20 min on the hall's terrace for the view. No tripods on or around the terrace.
items.about: A hall on a pillared terrace on the hillside, looking west over the whole Nara basin. It is named after the Shunie rite held here in the second month of the old calendar. Fire broke out during the rite in 1667, and the present hall was rebuilt two years later. It is a National Treasure.

items.detail: 10 min along the hillside from the Nigatsu-dō terrace. Allow 20–30 min. 🔴 It closes at 16:00, so go straight after lunch, before Kasuga Taisha. Aim to arrive by 14:45.
items.about: The oldest building at Tōdai-ji, older than the temple itself: it dates from 733. Inside, ten Nara-period statues, all National Treasures, stand close together around the Fukūkenjaku Kannon.

items.detail: 15–20 min through the deer park, then up the approach lined with lanterns. Worship at the outer hall is free. Allow 45 min–1 hour. Special worship inside the corridor: ¥700, desk open 9:00–16:00, so arrive by about 15:30. The special worship desk is closed in the morning on the 1st, 11th and 21st of each month and on the festival dates the shrine publishes. Today is none of them, and you arrive in the afternoon anyway.
items.about: Founded in 768 as the shrine of the Fujiwara family, and a World Heritage site. About 3,000 lanterns line the site: stone ones along the approach and bronze ones hanging in the corridors. The corridors and their lanterns are the main sight.

items.detail: 20 min downhill from the shrine, on the way to the station. Allow 1–1½ hours. The shops keep their own hours, so go about 16:30–17:30, no later. Skip it if you have had enough for the day; nothing later depends on it.
items.about: Nara's old merchant quarter: lanes of lattice-fronted townhouses, with red monkey charms hanging from the eaves.

transit.label: Walk — Naramachi to Kintetsu Nara
transit.detail: From Naramachi, 10 min on foot north up the arcade. From Kasuga Taisha, if you skip Naramachi: 25 min. Go to Kintetsu Nara: it has direct trains to Kyoto. JR Nara is a separate station about 1.1 km away.

transit.label: Kintetsu 17:44 express — Kintetsu Nara → Kyoto 18:36
transit.detail: Direct express, no change, about 50 min, no seat ticket needed. Direct expresses: 17:12 · 17:44 · 18:18 · 18:52 · 19:13. Limited expresses, 35 min, ¥520 seat ticket extra: 17:25 · 17:55 · 18:25. The last direct train is at 22:27, so there is no need to hurry. ⚑ If no Kintetsu trains are running: walk 20 min to JR Nara station and take a Miyakoji rapid to Kyoto, about 45 min.
transit.cost_note: one way; with this morning's ¥1,280 limited express, today's trains cost ¥2,040

backup.title: If it rains on Oct 31: go anyway
backup.detail: This day cannot swap with another: the Shōsō-in ticket is for 10:30 on this date. Rain only affects the walks between the halls and the open terrace at Nigatsu-dō. The exhibition and the Great Buddha Hall are indoors, and Kasuga Taisha's corridors are roofed.

title: Kurama to Kibune, and Sanjūsangen-dō

transit.label: JR + Keihan — Kyoto → Demachiyanagi
transit.detail: Leave the hotel at 07:45 for the 08:01 train. Take the JR Nara line one stop to Tōfukuji, then the Keihan line north to Demachiyanagi, the last stop: 20–30 min in all. You arrive at 08:30, in time for the 08:45 Eizan train up the mountain.
transit.cost_note: ¥150 JR + ¥300 Keihan

transit.label: Eizan line — Demachiyanagi → Kurama
transit.detail: About 30 min up the mountain, with a train every 15 min. ⚠ It is a Sunday in autumn-leaf season on one of Kyoto's most crowded local lines: expect to stand.
transit.cost_note: covers both Eizan rides: out to Kurama and back from Kibuneguchi

blocks.title: Up the switchback path (九十九折参道)

maps.label: Precinct and paths — Kurama-dera
maps.note: The temple's own guide to the mountain paths. Its front page is where a path closure would be posted.

maps.label: AllTrails — Kurama to Kibune
maps.note: Matches our line over the ridge. Route shape only — it is not a source for whether the path is open.

transit.label: On foot — Kurama Station → Yuki-jinja
transit.detail: 3 min from the station to the Niōmon gate. 💴 Pay the ¥500 mountain fee there, in cash. From the gate to the main hall is about 1 km of stone steps, with Yuki-jinja on the way. The temple says 30 min; allow 45. Before you start the climb: a cable car (¥200 donation, cash) runs up beside the path and saves the steps, but it stops above Yuki-jinja, so you would miss the shrine.

items.detail: Shrine on the path, a few minutes above the gate: the path runs straight through its worship hall. Allow 10–15 min; you see it from outside as you pass.
items.about: The guardian shrine of Kurama. Its worship hall, built in 1607, is split in two with the path running through the middle, a form called wari-haiden. The hall is an Important Cultural Property. So is the shrine's pair of guardian lion-dogs, which the shrine says are the only ones in Japan shown holding a child. The pair registered as an Important Cultural Property is reported to be kept at the Kyoto National Museum, with a faithful copy standing here. Look under their paws either way. The great cedar beside the hall is about 800 years old.

blocks.title: On up to the main hall

transit.label: On foot — Yuki-jinja → Kurama-dera
transit.detail: The rest of the climb up the switchback path. The 30–45 min for the climb from the gate to the main hall includes this part.

items.detail: Allow 20–30 min for the main hall and the courtyard in front of it. Then the Reihōden museum, 2 min further up: allow 30–45 min inside. ⚠ The Reihōden closes at 16:00 and is closed on Tuesdays. 💴 Cash only, here and at the gate.
items.about: In the courtyard in front of the main hall is the kongōshō, a stone mandala. The Reihōden is the temple's museum, on three small floors. The National Treasure Bishamonten triad is on the top floor.

blocks.title: Over the ridge (奥の院参道, the inner path)

transit.label: On foot — the inner path over the ridge (奥の院参道)
transit.detail: The temple's own training path. It starts behind the main hall and passes the Ikitsugi-no-mizu spring, the Sekurabe-ishi stone and the Kinone-michi, where cedar roots cover the surface of the path. From the main hall to the Nishi-mon gate at Kibune is about 3.9 km. Allow 60–90 min for the whole crossing. ⚠ It is a forest path of roots and stone. The temple advises not to go on after rain or when the light is going.

blocks.title: Down into Kibune (木の根道, the root path)

transit.label: On foot — the root path down to Kibune
transit.detail: Past the Ōsugi Gongen shrine and the Fudō-dō and Yoshitsune-dō halls to the Maō-den at the inner sanctuary. Then about 370 m of descent to the Nishi-mon gate. Kifune Shrine's Okunomiya (inner shrine) is a short way up the lane from the gate.

blocks.title: Kifune Shrine: three shrines, walked downhill

items.detail: Visit the three shrines from the top down: the Okunomiya (inner shrine) first, then the Yui-no-yashiro (middle shrine), then the Hongū (main shrine). This is the reverse of the usual order. You arrive from above, so it saves walking back uphill. Allow 40–60 min. Lunch is here, on the Kibune lane. ⏱ Sit down to lunch by 13:45. If you reach Denbe later than that, or there is a wait, skip it and eat at Demachiyanagi when you change trains. The riverside dining platforms are summer only and are not there in November.
items.about: At the Hongū, spring water runs out of a stone wall. Fortune slips floated on this water show their writing.

blocks.title: Down the valley and back into town

transit.label: On foot — down the valley road to Kibuneguchi
transit.detail: About 2 km down the valley road to Kibuneguchi station, past the ryokan street and the Hotaru-iwa rock. The shrine says 30 min, the temple 40. ⏱ Start walking down the valley by 14:30. Later than that, Sanjūsangen-dō is off for today: its last entry is 16:30. If you would rather ride: Kyoto Bus 33 covers the same stretch in about 5 min. It is a different company from the city buses, but you pay the same way: board at the back, tap once as you get off. If lunch runs past 14:30, take the bus instead of walking: it saves about 35 min. No timetable is listed, so don't count on one being due.

transit.label: Eizan line — Kibuneguchi → Demachiyanagi
transit.detail: About 28 min back down. The fare is included in the ¥940 shown on the ride out. Afternoon trains leave every 15 min, at :06, :21, :36 and :51 past the hour. The last train down leaves at 23:06, hours after you will need it.

transit.label: Keihan — Demachiyanagi → Shichijō
transit.detail: Keihan line from Demachiyanagi to Shichijō, then 7 min on foot to the hall.
transit.cost_note: estimate; covers this ride and the ride back to Kyoto Station

items.detail: Allow about an hour. You should arrive around 15:40. Last entry is 16:30, 30 min before closing (the 8:30–17:00 hours apply until 15 November).
items.about: A hall 120 m long holding 1,000 life-size statues of the Thousand-Armed Kannon. The great seated Kannon of 1254 is at the centre, with 28 attendant figures in front. The statues and the building are all National Treasures.

transit.label: Back to Kyoto Station
transit.detail: 7 min on foot to Shichijō station. Keihan line south to Tōfukuji, then change to the JR Nara line for one stop to Kyoto Station. This fare is in the ¥510 shown on the Keihan ride from Demachiyanagi. Or take a city bus west to Kyoto Station (board at the back, tap once as you get off); the bus fare is extra.

notes_top: 💴 Four small payments today, all cash: ¥500 mountain fee at the Niōmon gate, ¥200 donation if you take the cable car, ¥200 at the Reihōden museum, and ¥600 at Sanjūsangen-dō. Carry coins.

🛃 Japan's tax-free shopping rules change today, Nov 1. From now on you pay the full price, including tax, and the tax is refunded only after customs at Narita confirms the goods are leaving Japan, on your departure morning. What you bought on the two Tokyo shopping days falls under the old rules and needs nothing. From today, only buy tax-free if you are willing to spend time on it at Narita on departure morning.

backup.title: If it rains: swap with the Uji day, or skip the ridge path
backup.detail: Check the Weather page on the evening of Sat Oct 31, for both Sun Nov 1 and Fri Nov 6. Rule: if Nov 1 shows a rain chance of 70% or more and 10 mm or more for the day, or a typhoon heading for Kyoto, swap this day with Fri Nov 6 (Uji), which is almost all indoors. Swap only if Nov 6 looks drier, and only if you have not already used Nov 6 for another rainy day. If Nov 6 is taken, swap with Mon Nov 2 (the Kamo shrines, about half under cover) instead. Dinner does not move: on each date, eat at the restaurant listed for that date; both are a few minutes from the hotel. On Sunday Byōdō-in is busier, so be at the Phoenix Hall ticket desk, inside the garden, when it opens at 09:10. The Kurama day also works on a Friday: the Reihōden museum closes only on Tuesdays, and Denbe, the soba shop for lunch, closes on Thursdays. Weekday train times differ, so check them on the day. Before you leave the hotel, check the Eizan Railway website (eizandensha.co.jp): in heavy rain the line can stop running. If it is not running, swap the day as above. Showers or light rain: keep the day, but skip the ridge path. Pay the ¥500 mountain fee at the Niōmon gate as planned. 2 min past the gate, take the temple's cable car from Sanmon station (山門駅) up to Tahōtō station (多宝塔駅). It runs every 20 min from 08:40, takes 2 min and costs a ¥200 donation in cash. You miss Yuki-jinja this way. From the top station it is 10 min on foot up to the main hall. See the main hall and the Reihōden museum, which is indoors. Take the cable car back down (last car 16:25) and walk 3 min to Kurama station. Take the Eizan line one stop, to Kibuneguchi. Then take Kyoto Bus 33 up the valley to Kibune, about 5 min; board at the back and tap once as you get off. If no bus is due, walk the paved road up instead: about 2 km, 30–40 min. Both fares are extra to the ¥940 shown on the Eizan ride. From the bus stop, walk up the paved lane to the Hongū (main shrine), then on to the Yui-no-yashiro (middle shrine) and the Okunomiya (inner shrine). Walk back down the lane for lunch, then go on to Sanjūsangen-dō as planned. If rain starts during the day, check the ridge path when you reach the main hall. If it is raining or the path is wet, don't walk it: the temple advises against it after rain. Take the cable car down and go to Kibune by train and bus, as above. If rain starts once you are on the ridge path, the only ways off it are back to the main hall or on to Kibune. From the Maō-den, the top of the path, the temple gives 20 min down to Kifune Shrine. Walk slowly on the roots and stones.

transit.label: City bus — Kyoto Station → Tadasu-no-Mori (Shimogamo Shrine)
transit.detail: Leave the hotel at about 08:45. The bus takes about 30 min north across the city, to the point where two rivers meet at the south end of the Shimogamo Shrine forest.
transit.payment: Board by the REAR door; don't tap your card on the way in. Pay as you get off: one tap on the reader beside the driver, then leave by the front door. The city fare is a flat ¥230, so it is one tap however far you ride. If your card balance is too low, the same box takes cash.

items.detail: The forest approach to Shimogamo Shrine. Walk north through it to the shrine: about 0.7 km on the flat, 15–20 min. Walk it slowly; the forest is the sight.
items.about: Tadasu-no-Mori is 12 hectares of forest that has never been cleared. It is a National Historic Site and lies inside the World Heritage area of Shimogamo Shrine.

items.detail: Small shrine near the south end of the Tadasu-no-Mori forest. Allow 15–20 min. It closes at 16:30, earlier than the main shrine, so it is the one to see first if you arrive late.
items.about: Kawai-jinja is the most important of Shimogamo's subsidiary shrines. The writer Kamo no Chōmei grew up here; his father was its senior priest. Its votive tablets are shaped like hand mirrors, and visitors decorate the face on them with their own make-up.

items.detail: Allow 45 min–1¼ hours for the main hall, the small shrines around it, the pond and the bridge. The paid area opens at 10:00. If you go in, add 30–45 min.
items.about: The main hall is a National Treasure, best seen from the chūmon (middle gate). Around it stand seven small shrines for the signs of the Chinese zodiac. Beyond them are the Mitarashi pond and an arched bridge. The paid area has three things to see: the Ōi-dono, the hall that was the kitchen where food for the gods was prepared; the carriage house, with material on the Aoi Matsuri festival; and a rebuilt copy of the hut, ten feet square, in which Kamo no Chōmei wrote the Hōjōki.

transit.label: On foot — up the river to Kamigamo
transit.detail: 3.5–4 km on the path beside the river. The Aoi Matsuri festival procession takes this same route in the same direction. About 40 min of walking, or about 1 hour with road crossings and stops. Have lunch somewhere along this walk.

items.detail: Allow 30 min–1 hour for the open grounds. The priest-guided visit to the inner court runs 9:00–16:00 on this date, costs ¥1,000 and takes 20–30 min. You don't need to book for one person. ⚠ The shrine says the inner-court visit is often stopped or moved to other times for religious ceremonies. Ask at the shrine office when you arrive whether it is running today. If it is not running: nothing else changes. The grounds, the sand cones and the Shake-machi lane are all still open.
items.about: Kamigamo and Shimogamo are Kyoto's two Kamo shrines. In front of the Hosodono hall stand two cones of raked sand. Also look for the rōmon (two-storey gate) and the smaller shrines along the stream, which are Important Cultural Properties. The inner-court visit includes the story of the Kamo gods, told in the Naoraiden hall, the treasure display in the Takakuradono, and a view of the main hall, a National Treasure, with a second hall of the same design beside it. From 31 October to 6 December the visit is part of Kyoto's autumn opening of cultural sites that are normally closed to the public. That is why it costs ¥1,000 instead of the usual ¥500; the halls you see are the same.

items.detail: A lane of old priests' houses, 2 min from the Kamigamo gate. About 500 m long, outside only, 20–30 min. ⏱ Be on the bus west by 15:00: Sōken-in takes its last visitors at 16:00 and Kōrin-in at 16:30. If Kamigamo has taken longer than planned: skip this lane.
items.about: The Shake-machi was home to the shrine's own families of priests. It follows the Myōjin-gawa stream as it flows out of the shrine grounds, past earthen bridges and walls, gates and front gardens. The houses have a gable detail found only on houses here. The lane is a nationally selected preservation district.

transit.label: City bus — Kamigamo → Daitoku-ji
transit.detail: Take bus 37 or bus 9, whichever comes first, west from the Misonobashi stop to Kitaōji-Horikawa (8 min). Then walk about 10 min east along Kitaōji street to the temple gate. Allow 20–30 min in all, with the wait. If no bus is coming: walk about 20 min east to Kitayama station, take the subway one stop to Kitaōji, then walk about 15 min west to the temple.
transit.payment: REAR door in, nothing to do. One tap on the reader beside the driver as you leave by the front door. Flat ¥230. If the card is short, the same box takes cash.

items.detail: Allow 30–40 min. See this temple first: it stops letting visitors in at 16:00, half an hour before Kōrin-in. 💴 Cash only.
items.about: Sōken-in is the memorial temple of Oda Nobunaga. Hideyoshi built it in 1583, one year after Nobunaga died at Honnō-ji. Building it was also a way for Hideyoshi to stake his claim as Nobunaga's successor. Inside is the life-size seated statue of Nobunaga that Hideyoshi had made, an Important Cultural Property. There are also seven grave markers of the Oda family and three tea rooms.

items.detail: Allow 30–40 min; last entry 16:30. Leave time to sit at the dry garden. 💴 Cash only.
items.about: Kōrin-in was founded in the 1520s by the Hatakeyama family. Later Maeda Toshiie had it re-roofed and made it his own family's temple as well. The front gate and the main hall, with its Chinese-style gate, survive from the founding and are Important Cultural Properties. The main hall's low roof makes it look calm and settled. The dry garden is white sand with groups of stones.

items.detail: Free, with no set opening hours. Allow 15–25 min to walk around it; you see the buildings from outside. The abbot's hall (honbō) is normally closed.
items.about: Walking through, you pass the imperial messenger gate, the Sanmon (main gate) with the upper storey Rikyū added in 1589, the Buddha hall and the Dharma hall, all seen from outside, and the lanes between the sub-temples. The abbot's hall and the Chinese-style gate brought from Hideyoshi's Jurakudai palace are National Treasures. Both belong to the honbō, which is why they are not on the walk.

transit.label: City bus — Daitoku-ji → Kyoto Station
transit.detail: Bus 206 south across the city from the Daitokuji-mae stop: about 40 min, one every 8 min or so. If you prefer the subway: walk 15 min east to Kitaōji station on the Karasuma line. That way Kyoto Station is about 30 min from the temple gate.
transit.payment: REAR door in, nothing to do. One tap on the reader beside the driver as you leave by the front door. Flat ¥230. If the card is short, the same box takes cash.

backup.title: If it rains: take the bus between the shrines
backup.detail: Both shrines and the Daitoku-ji sub-temples are fine to visit in rain. What rain spoils is the 3.5 km riverside walk between the two shrines. Take a bus between them instead. The day still works, just a little shorter. If Fri Oct 30, Sun Nov 1 or Tue Nov 3 is forecast wet, you can swap that day with this one. ⚑ This day is only a partial answer to rain: about half of it is under cover. The Ikaruga day (Thu Oct 29) is the one that can fill a whole wet day, so swap this day in only when heavy rain is forecast.

title: Takao & Jingo-ji

transit.label: JR Sagano line — Kyoto → Saga-Arashiyama
transit.detail: Leave the hotel at 07:45 to reach Saga-Arashiyama a little after 08:00. From there you walk all the way out of the city to the temples at Takao. The walk is what this day is for. If you want to be home about an hour earlier, leave at 07:20 instead. That start lets you catch the 16:14 bus back instead of the 16:54 (see the bus at the end of the day).
transit.cost_note: Kyoto → Saga-Arashiyama

blocks.title: Out of the city on foot: Kyoto Trail, Nishiyama course (京都一周トレイル 西山コース)

maps.label: Kyoto Trail, Nishiyama course — Kyoto City
maps.note: The city's own course page: Takao–Kiyotaki–Toriimoto–Arashiyama, our exact line written the other way round. Has an elevation profile; the printed guide map is sold separately.

maps.label: AllTrails — Kiyotaki to Jingo-ji
maps.note: The middle stretch only. It does not include the walk out of Arashiyama, nor Saimyō-ji and Kōzan-ji.

transit.label: On foot — Saga-Arashiyama Station → Toriimoto
transit.detail: Allow 55–70 min for the whole walk from the station to Kiyotaki. That time includes the next stretch, from Toriimoto over the pass. The marked route leaves town through Toriimoto, then crosses the old Kokoromi-tōge pass road over the top of the Kiyotaki tunnel. You do not walk through the road tunnel.

items.detail: Old street of wooden houses on the walk out of town, about 600 m long. Open street with no gate. You pass through about 08:30. The city's free preservation hall on the street opens at 10:00, so it will still be shut.
items.about: Saga Toriimoto grew up as a temple-gate town on the pilgrims’ road to the Atago shrine on the mountain above. It was chosen as a national preservation district in 1979. Townhouses (machiya) with mushiko lattice windows stand next to thatched farmhouses.

blocks.title: Over the pass to Kiyotaki (清滝)

transit.label: On foot — Toriimoto → Kiyotaki
transit.detail: Over the old Kokoromi-tōge pass road and down into the village of Kiyotaki. The 55–70 min given for the walk from the station includes this stretch.

items.detail: Small village on the river, where the gorge walk to Takao starts. ⚠ There is no toilet between here and Takao-bashi bridge.
items.about: Kiyotaki was the overnight stop for pilgrims climbing Atago-yama. The Watarizaru and Kinrei bridges cross the river here. Upstream, towards Takao, the gorge is called Kin’unkei. Downstream it is called Kinreikei.

transit.label: On foot — Kiyotaki → Jingo-ji
transit.detail: About 3 km along the valley floor, almost flat. Allow about 2 hours. It is easy enough for beginners. ⚠ The rock underfoot is slippery after rain. At Takao-bashi bridge, climb about 350 stone steps to the Jingo-ji gate: 10–30 min, depending on your legs.

items.detail: You arrive about 11:30, well before the 16:00 close. Allow 50–70 min. See the Kondō (main hall) with its National Treasure Yakushi Nyorai statue, and the pagoda. Then throw small clay discs off the Jizō-in terrace into the gorge below. The Daishi-dō hall is open only 1–7 November, 09:00–16:00, for ¥500 on top of the entry ticket. It shows a carved wooden statue of Kōbō Daishi that is not on view at any other time. Allow 20–30 min more for it. The temple prints those dates without a year, so the 2026 opening is likely but not certain.
items.about: Jingo-ji is a mountain temple of the Shingon school of Buddhism. The Yakushi Nyorai (the Medicine Buddha) in the Kondō is a National Treasure. The custom of throwing clay discs off a terrace began here, at Jizō-in. The Kōbō Daishi statue in the Daishi-dō is an Important Cultural Property.

blocks.title: Down to Takao-bashi bridge and north to Saimyō-ji

transit.label: On foot — Jingo-ji → Saimyō-ji
transit.detail: Back down the steps: 10–15 min. Stop for lunch on the way down. The two teahouses stand on the steps themselves, about half way down, above the bridge. Takao’s riverside dining platforms are summer-only and are gone by November. From the bridge, walk 20 min north along the river road to Saimyō-ji. ⏱ Leave Takao-bashi bridge by 14:50 to see both Saimyō-ji and Kōzan-ji before Kōzan-ji closes at 17:00. If you are later: skip Saimyō-ji and walk straight on to Kōzan-ji (40 min). If you cannot leave the bridge by 15:25: skip Kōzan-ji too, walk on to the Toganoo stop and take a bus; buses run until 20:04.

items.detail: Small temple across the vermilion Shigetsu bridge. Allow 25–35 min. The guest hall has a special opening from late October to the end of November, so it should be open today. The visit is still worth it if it is shut.
items.about: The main hall dates from 1700. Inside are a standing Shakyamuni (the historical Buddha) attributed to the sculptor Unkei, a thousand-armed Kannon from the Heian period and an Aizen Myōō from the Kamakura period. A moss garden is seen from inside the hall.

transit.label: On foot — Saimyō-ji → Kōzan-ji
transit.detail: 20 min further up the road to Toganoo, where Kōzan-ji stands.

items.detail: World Heritage temple and the last stop of the day. Allow 40–55 min. See the Sekisui-in hall, the founder’s hall and the tea garden. 🔴 Kōzan-ji closes at 17:00, and that is the deadline for the day. You should arrive about 14:50, or about 15:20 if you visited the Daishi-dō at Jingo-ji. To see it all before closing, arrive by 16:05. That gives you about 1 hour 15 min to spare, or about 45 min if you visited the Daishi-dō.
items.about: Kōzan-ji is part of the Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto World Heritage site. The Sekisui-in, a National Treasure, is the only building left from the monk Myōe’s time. It began as the temple’s east sutra repository, took the name Sekisui-in after the original hall of that name was lost in a flood in 1228, and in 1889 was moved here and altered into residential form. The Chōjū-giga scroll on show is a copy; the originals are not normally displayed. A stone in the tea garden reads “Japan’s oldest tea garden”. The temple’s own website says the oldest garden was across the Kiyotaki river, and that this plot held a monks’ hall. So the stone is a monument, and this is not the actual spot.

transit.label: Bus — Toganoo → Kyoto Station
transit.detail: The bus stop is 3 min on foot from the Kōzan-ji gate. It is the first stop on the route of Kyoto City Bus 8, so buses start here empty. Once you are on, you get a seat. If the bus fills up, you may have to wait for the next one. If you visited the Daishi-dō: take the 16:54 City Bus 8. It reaches Shijō-Ōmiya at 17:39 and Shijō-Karasuma, the last stop, a few minutes later. Then take the Karasuma subway 2 stops to Kyoto, and you are at the hotel about 17:55. Dinner is at Kyoto Station with last orders at 21:00, so this bus leaves plenty of time. If you skipped the Daishi-dō, or left the hotel at 07:20: take the 16:14 West Japan JR Bus instead. It goes straight to the bus terminal in front of Kyoto Station, arriving 17:11. If you miss your bus: 12 more buses leave after the 16:54 on the two lines, and the last is the 20:04 JR Bus. Both lines run the same timetable every day of the week, so the 3 November holiday changes nothing.
transit.payment: Both bus companies work the same way, so it does not matter which bus you caught. Board by the rear door and do nothing yet. Tap your card once on the reader beside the driver as you leave by the front door. Both take Suica (the JR bus has since 2015). Flat fare on both: ¥230. If your card is short of money, the same reader box takes cash.
transit.cost_note: flat fare on either bus company, because Takao is inside Kyoto’s flat-fare zone; the 2 Karasuma subway stops after City Bus 8 cost extra

notes_top: ⚠ Two safety rules for the walk in, both posted on the trail’s own signs. First: walking through the Kiyotaki road tunnel is strictly forbidden. Take the old Kokoromi-tōge pass road over the top instead, which is the route this day uses. Second: since July there has been a bear-sighting warning near trail marker 87. That is at the Takao end of the Kitayama-West course, close to today’s route. It is a warning, and the trail is not closed. Today’s route follows the valley floor, a popular riverside path, in full daylight, and all the walking is done by about 15:50. Carry a bell and make noise as you walk. Stay off the trail at first light and at dusk; today’s timings keep you off it at both.
💴 Bring cash. The Jingo-ji gate, the extra Daishi-dō fee and the Takao teahouses do not take cards. Both buses back into the city take Suica; board at the rear door.

backup.title: If it rains: skip the walk and take the bus to the temples
backup.detail: Of all the days on the trip, rain hurts this one most. ⚠ The gorge path is officially slippery when wet, and the walk from Saga-Arashiyama through Kiyotaki is the first half of the day. If the forecast is wet: skip the walk and take the bus straight up to the temples. Jingo-ji, Saimyō-ji and Kōzan-ji all work in rain and are worth the trip on their own. You keep the temples, but you lose the walk, which is the main point of the day. ⚑ Swapping days barely helps. Oct 29, Oct 31 and Nov 2 are already behind you by this morning, so Uji on Nov 6 is the only day left to swap with, and only if you have not already used it for Oct 30 or Nov 1. That would put the Kansai day most at risk from rain on your last day before you move to Hiroshima, with no second chance if that day is wet too.

title: Daigo-ji, Tōfuku-ji & the Fushimi Inari loop

transit.label: JR — Kyoto → Yamashina
transit.detail: Leave the hotel at about 08:30, so you reach Sanbō-in as it opens at 09:00. Change at Yamashina to the Tōzai subway line, because the Tōzai line does not run to Kyoto Station.
transit.cost_note: one way; ¥360 return

transit.label: Kyoto subway, Tōzai line — Yamashina → Daigo
transit.detail: From Daigo station it is about 10 min on foot to the temple gate. Hotel to gate takes 20–30 min in all.
transit.cost_note: one way; ¥520 return

items.detail: Go here first. Every Daigo-ji ticket is sold at the Sanbō-in reception, and the other areas do not sell tickets. Buy the tickets for all the areas you want here, in one go, on the way in. Allow 45 min–1 hour.
items.about: The residence of Daigo-ji's abbots, founded in 1115. Two of its buildings are National Treasures. The Omote-shoin is the hall facing the garden; the floor mats of its lower room lift away to reveal a Noh stage. The Kara-mon gate was opened only for messengers from the emperor. The garden is both a Special Historic Site and a Special Place of Scenic Beauty. Toyotomi Hideyoshi drew its design himself in 1598, for his flower-viewing party at Daigo.

blocks.title: The lower precinct: the Garan (main halls) and the Reihōkan (treasure house)

items.detail: Allow 45 min–1 hour for the Kondō (main hall) and the five-storey pagoda. Then the Reihōkan treasure house: 30–45 min. It has three rooms, and one of them is open all year, so there is always something on show.
items.about: The Kondō and the five-storey pagoda stand side by side, and both are National Treasures. The Kondō was first built by order of Emperor Daigo in 926. Under Hideyoshi it was rebuilt with a hall brought from Kishū (today's Wakayama). The pagoda was finished in 951 and is the oldest wooden building in Kyoto Prefecture. The mandalas painted on its first storey are a source of Japanese esoteric Buddhist painting. The Reihōkan's collection is very large.

blocks.title: Kami-Daigo (upper Daigo): only if the mountain path has reopened

items.detail: ⛔ Closed since June 2026 (last checked 4 September 2026). The front page of Daigo-ji's website says entry to the upper mountain is forbidden for now, because part of the path may collapse. Check that page on the morning of 4 November. If the notice is still there: skip this card and go on to Tōfuku-ji and Fushimi Inari as planned. If the notice has gone: do this climb instead of the afternoon plan (Tōfuku-ji and Fushimi Inari). Eat first: the lunch you bought at Kyoto Station, because the temple restaurant is closed. Sign the entry register at the Nyonin-dō trailhead, which is open 09:00–15:00. Start by 12:30. It is about 1 hour up on zigzag stone steps, and 2–2½ hours for the round trip including the halls. The temple asks you to be back at the foot by 17:00. No separate fee for the mountain is published. Entry can be refused in bad weather.
items.about: There is no view at the top; you climb for the halls. The Yakushi-dō and the haiden (worship hall) of Kiyotaki-gū are both National Treasures. Beside them are the Nyoirin-dō and the Kaisan-dō (founder's hall), which Toyotomi Hideyori rebuilt in 1606. The Daigo spring is also at the top, and its water can still be drunk.

transit.label: Tōzai line, then JR — Daigo → Tōfukuji, changing at Rokujizō
transit.detail: Take the 13:29 Tōzai line train two stops to Rokujizō. Change to the JR Nara line, northbound, to Tōfukuji, arriving 13:52. That is 23 min with one change. If you miss the 13:29, trains run about every 10 min. The temple is about 10 min on foot south of Tōfukuji station. ⛔ Only if the Kami-Daigo landslide notice has gone from Daigo-ji's website on the morning of 4 November: climb Kami-Daigo instead of taking this train. The entry register at the Nyonin-dō trailhead is open 09:00–15:00. The climb is about 1 hour each way on zigzag stone steps, and the temple asks you to be back at the foot by 17:00. On 4 September 2026 the mountain was closed, and had been since June.
transit.cost_note: one way, IC; ¥260 subway + ¥160 JR

items.detail: Arrive about 14:00. Reception closes at 16:00, and there is no re-entry. You have about 1 hour 15 min inside: leave the gate by 15:20 to catch the 15:30 train (Tōfukuji station is 10 min on foot). If you miss it, the next train is 15:37. The Sanmon gate is seen from outside only. Two areas are paid, both on one ¥1,000 ticket: the Tsūten-kyō bridge, leading to the founder's hall, and the abbot's hall with its gardens. The autumn viewing period starts on 14 November, so today normal prices apply and there is no crowd control.
items.about: A large Zen temple. The Sanmon (main gate) is a National Treasure. The Zen meditation hall of 1347 and the Tōsu (monks' latrine) beside it are the oldest buildings of their kind in Japan. The Tsūten-kyō is a covered bridge across a ravine full of maples, leading to the founder's hall. The abbot's hall has four gardens round it, laid out by the garden designer Shigemori Mirei in 1939. The best known is the north garden, a checkerboard of re-used paving stones.

transit.label: JR Nara line — Tōfukuji → Inari
transit.detail: One stop, 2 min. Trains at 15:30, 15:37 and 15:48. The street leading to the shrine starts outside Inari station. Go straight up to the shrine. There is no time for lunch before the mountain loop.
transit.cost_note: one way, IC

items.detail: The loop over Inari-yama (Mount Inari) is about 4 km, with 233 m of climbing, mostly on steps. Allow 2–2½ hours. Route: through the Rōmon gate and past the main hall, then up through the Senbon Torii (the rows of torii gates) to Yotsutsuji, where the city opens out below. From there, go round the summit peaks (Ichi-no-mine is the highest) and come down the other side of the loop, back to Yotsutsuji. There is no gate and no closing time. People climb day and night, so coming down at dusk with the lanterns lit is normal here. ⚠ Sunset is 17:01. Be past the summit by about 16:45, so that you are on the lower slopes as it gets dark. ⏱ If you are not at Yotsutsuji by 16:15, do not go on to the summit. Turn back there and walk down (about 30 min). If you are tired: go up to Yotsutsuji and back, about 1 hour. 🔴 Shrine rule: eat only in the marked rest areas, never while walking.
items.about: The head shrine of about 30,000 Inari shrines across Japan. The whole mountain is the shrine's grounds. About 10,000 torii gates line the mountain paths. Since the Edo period, people have donated them in thanks for prayers answered. The main hall was rebuilt in 1499, after the whole shrine burned down in the Ōnin war.

transit.label: JR Nara line — Inari → Kyoto
transit.detail: Two stops, 5 min, straight into Kyoto Station. Trains at 17:40, 17:50, 17:57, then about every 10 min. Trains run late, so there is no risk of missing the last one: 20:46, 21:03, 22:45, 23:08 and 23:34 all run on Wednesdays.
transit.cost_note: one way, IC

backup.title: If it rains: drop the Inari mountain loop
backup.detail: Rain makes little difference to the morning: Sanbō-in and its garden, the Kondō and the pagoda, and the whole treasure house. At Tōfuku-ji the bridge is covered, and you see the abbot's hall gardens from its verandas. The Inari loop is the part to drop: two hours on wet stone steps is not worth it. Instead, see the shrine's Rōmon gate, the main hall and the first stretch of torii gates, about 30 min, and end the day early. This is a moderate loss: you lose the walk, and you still see every building.

title: The Yoshino ridge

blocks.title: South to Yoshino, and up to the village

transit.label: Kintetsu 07:06 — Kyoto → Yoshino 09:22, changing at Kashiharajingū-mae
transit.detail: Leave the hotel at 06:45. The Kintetsu ticket gates are on the south side of Kyoto Station, about 10 min away. The hotel breakfast opens at 06:30, too late to sit down to: buy breakfast at a konbini on the way and eat it on the train. Take the 07:06 express south and change at Kashiharajingū-mae.
