It arrives at Yoshino at 09:22, in time for the 09:35 ropeway car up the hill. This is the cheapest train that gets you up the hill by about 09:45. The trip takes 2 hours 16 min each way, so you spend about 4½ hours on trains today, the most of any day trip on this holiday. No train arrives earlier. The limited expresses cost ¥3,070 instead of ¥1,480, and the fastest one arrives at 09:26. Taking one lets you leave Kyoto later, at 07:30, but you arrive at about the same time. If you miss the 07:06: the next ¥1,480 train is the 07:34, arriving 09:52, for the 10:05 car. You reach the top 30 min later.
transit.cost_note: one way; ¥2,960 the round trip

transit.label: Ropeway — Yoshino Station → Kinpusen-ji
transit.detail: The ropeway's lower station, Senbonguchi, is 3 min on foot from the platform. From 23 October to 30 November the ropeway runs every day, so it runs today, and the replacement minibus is not running. Cars leave every 15 min, at :05, :20, :35 and :50, from 09:20 until the last car at 17:20. The ride takes about 3 min, and extra cars run when it is busy. Take the 09:35. If the queue is long: walk up the Nanamagari slope instead. It takes 30–35 min. From the upper station, walk uphill about 15 min to the Zaō-dō, the main hall of Kinpusen-ji.
transit.payment: 💴 Have cash ready: ¥500 one way, ¥900 return. The operator does not say whether it takes IC cards.
transit.cost_note: one way; ¥900 return

items.detail: This is the main reason for the day. Allow 1–1½ hours. 🔴 The three Kongō Zaō Gongen statues are on show for the autumn opening, 24 October to 30 November 2026. The central one is over 7 m tall. An exhibition of paintings by Matsuda Daiji is on at the same time, in the Okuden Honji-dō hall. ⚠ During services the hall may close to visitors for a short time. ⚠ The Niōmon gate is under repair until 2028 and cannot be seen. Its two Niō statues are not on view anywhere during this trip.
items.about: Head temple of Kinpusen Shugen Honshū and the centre of Shugendō, the mountain religion. The Zaō-dō (main hall) is a National Treasure. The temple says that among Japan's ancient wooden buildings, only the Great Buddha Hall at Tōdai-ji is bigger. Inside stands what the temple calls the largest shrine cabinet in the country. It holds the three Kongō Zaō Gongen statues. The Niōmon gate is the temple's other National Treasure. It is being taken apart and repaired until 2028. Its two 5 m Niō statues were moved to a museum for the repair, and that museum's sculpture hall closes in September 2026.

items.detail: Next to Kinpusen-ji. Allow about 30 min. The shoin (the old residence hall) is the reason to visit. ⚠ The gate is open until 17:00, but the shoin and the seal desk close at 16:30. The Hitome Senbon viewpoint is in the grounds, beside the car park. Have lunch nearby after this visit, in the Naka-senbon area. The eateries on the mountain close in the late afternoon, so lunch is on the mountain and dinner is back in Kyoto.
items.about: The shrine calls itself the only surviving temporary palace of the Southern Court. The shoin is an Important Cultural Property. The shrine calls it the oldest surviving example of shoin-style residential architecture in Japan. Look for the unusually wide, shallow alcove, the staggered shelves held up with no strut, and the nail covers made of wood instead of metal. Three famous stories took place in the same rooms. In 1185 Yoshitsune, Shizuka Gozen and Benkei hid here. In 1336 Emperor Go-Daigo made the building his palace. In 1594 Hideyoshi held a flower-viewing party here. Noh masks and gold screens from that party are on show. Hitome Senbon means “a thousand cherries at a glance”.

maps.label: Walking map — Yoshinoyama Tourist Association
maps.note: Two sheets: the whole ridge from Shimo-senbon to Kami-senbon, and a second one for the Oku-senbon beyond it. Shows the climbs and walking times.

maps.label: AllTrails — Mikumari shrine loop
maps.note: 12 km, 4–4.5 hours, and it names Kinpusen-ji and Mikumari. Drawn as a loop; ours is one way, up the ridge and down the village road.

transit.label: On foot — Yoshimizu-jinja → Yoshino Mikumari-jinja
transit.detail: 1 hour 10 min, with about 270 m of climbing in total. You walk up the paved village road, past the Hanayagura viewpoint. Temples, shops and lodgings line the road the whole way, so you can stop or turn back every few hundred metres. ⚑ A phone map shows no trail name here. Yoshino gives names to its areas and none to its paths. You walk up through Naka-senbon (中千本) into Kami-senbon (上千本). Oku-senbon (奥千本) is the top. Find your way by the three shrines: Yoshimizu (吉水神社), Yoshino Mikumari (吉野水分神社) and Kinpu (金峯神社).

items.detail: Allow about 20 min. ⚠ The grounds close at 16:00. ⏱ Go on up to Kinpu-jinja only if you leave here by 13:45. Otherwise start down from here. If you are still here at 14:30, start down at once: at the slow end the walk down takes 1½ hours.
items.about: A complete shrine compound from the Momoyama period, in Kami-senbon. The main hall, offering hall, worship hall, tower gate and cloister are all listed together as Important Cultural Properties. The three shrines of the main hall stand under one long roof. Toyotomi Hideyori rebuilt the shrine in 1604. His father, Hideyoshi, had prayed here for a child, and Hideyori was born. The seated statue of Tamayori-hime, a National Treasure, is not on show.

blocks.title: Optional: up to Oku-senbon (奥千本), the top of the village

transit.label: On foot — Yoshino Mikumari-jinja → Kinpu-jinja
transit.detail: Optional. The day is complete without it. 25–30 min up from Yoshino Mikumari-jinja, then a loop of about 40 min. ⏱ Only go up if you leave Yoshino Mikumari-jinja by 13:45. From 23 October to 30 November the Oku-senbon bus runs every day, so it runs today. It is only useful for the way down. It leaves Oku-senbon-guchi (奥千本口), the last stop, below Kinpu-jinja, at 14:08 and 15:08. It goes to Chikurin-in-mae (竹林院前) in Naka-senbon. 💴 The fare is ¥400, cash only, paid on board. The 15:08 is the last bus. If you miss it, walk down. Walking down is the plan anyway if you don't use the bus.

items.detail: Allow 20–30 min. Free, with no gate, so you can visit at any hour.
items.about: The Shugendō summit shrine, at the top of the village road. The Engishiki register lists it as a major shrine. It is the shrine of the guardian god of the whole Kinpusen range. People pray to him as a god who keeps living things from withering, and, because the mountain was said to hold gold ore, as a god of gold. A little below the shrine buildings stands a tower. Yoshitsune is said to have hidden in it, and then kicked his way out through the roof.

transit.label: On foot — down the village road
transit.detail: All downhill from Kinpu-jinja, 1 hour 15 min to 1½ hours, back through Kami-senbon and Naka-senbon to the ropeway's upper station below the Zaō-dō. Sunset today is 17:00, and last light (civil dusk) is 17:26. The last ropeway car down leaves at 17:20. If you skip the top, you leave Yoshino Mikumari-jinja at about 13:45 and reach the ropeway at about 15:15. That is about 1¾ hours before sunset and 2 hours before the last car. If you go to the top, you reach the ropeway by about 16:25. Daylight runs out before the ropeway stops, so watch the daylight. ⏱ If you are still at Yoshino Mikumari-jinja at 14:30, start down then. At the slow end the walk down takes 1½ hours.

transit.label: Ropeway — down from the village to Yoshino Station
transit.detail: Board at the ropeway's upper station, below the Zaō-dō. You do not need to climb back up to the temple. Cars run every 15 min. The last car down is at 17:20, 20 min after sunset. If you miss it: walk down the Nanamagari slope, which needs no service. The ropeway operator itself gives this walk as the alternative.
transit.payment: 💴 ¥500 in cash, unless you bought the ¥900 return at the bottom.
transit.cost_note: one way; ¥900 return

transit.label: Kintetsu — Yoshino → Kyoto
transit.detail: If you reach the ropeway at about 15:15, the 15:20 car gets you to Yoshino Station at about 15:26. Take the 15:38, arriving Kyoto 17:51, on the ¥1,480 fare. Or take the 15:34: it arrives about 20 min sooner, but needs a second change and a limited-express ticket, ¥2,000 or more. The last train from Yoshino is at 21:30, so a slow afternoon costs you nothing. Have dinner back in Kyoto: the eateries on the mountain close early.
transit.cost_note: one way; ¥2,960 the round trip

notes_top: 💴 Carry ¥6,500 or more in cash this morning. The ropeway is ¥500 each way and does not say it takes cards. Kinpusen-ji is ¥1,600. Yoshimizu-jinja is ¥600. Lunch at Yakko, the persimmon-leaf sushi restaurant, is ¥1,000–1,999, cash. The optional Oku-senbon bus is ¥400, cash only. The kuzu sweets at Nakai Shunpū-dō are ¥900.

backup.title: If it rains: swap the whole day for Taima-dera
backup.detail: This day is a walk along a village road on a ridge, and the walk is the point. Rain spoils the whole day, so swap all of it. Spend a full day at Taima-dera instead. It is a shorter day, mostly under cover. It is on the same Kintetsu Minami-Osaka line, 15 min on foot from Taimadera station. Admission is ¥1,000. The temple says it is the only one in Japan where both of its ancient pagodas, East and West, still stand. The two pagodas and the Mandara-dō main hall are all National Treasures. It is a much weaker day than the ridge walk.

title: Uji — Byōdō-in & Manpuku-ji

transit.label: JR Nara line — Kyoto → Uji
transit.detail: Leave the hotel at 08:30. The rapid train to Uji takes about 20 min, then it is 10 min on foot to Byōdō-in. 🔴 Arrive before 09:30. Tickets to go inside the Phoenix Hall are for set times, sold on the day only, and cannot be booked. Arriving early is how you get a time slot.
transit.cost_note: this is the whole day's JR fare, for all three rides: Kyoto → Uji, Uji → Ōbaku and Ōbaku → Kyoto

items.detail: Allow 1½–2 hours in all. 🔴 Go first to the Phoenix Hall interior desk, inside the garden, and buy your ticket to go inside the hall. The desk opens at 09:10 and sells tickets first come, first served. Groups go in every 20 min, from 09:30 to 16:10. Tickets can sell out well before the last group, and on some days religious services stop interior visits altogether. Then see the garden and the Hōshōkan museum before or after your time slot. ⚠ The Kannon-dō hall is behind a building-site barrier for the rest of the year, and you cannot go near it. It is a minor building. The Phoenix Hall and the museum are open as normal. ⏱ If your time slot is late: leave Byōdō-in by 15:00 to fit in both Ujigami-jinja and Manpuku-ji (reception closes at 16:30). If you leave after 15:00, skip Manpuku-ji. You can still reach Ujigami-jinja before its last entry at 16:10 if you leave Byōdō-in by 15:40.
items.about: Byōdō-in is a World Heritage temple on the Uji river, and the building on Japan's ten-yen coin. The Hōshōkan museum holds the Phoenix Hall's original fittings and displays the temple's National Treasures. The Kannon-dō is an Important Cultural Property from the mid-Kamakura period. It is having its first major repair since 1922, and is expected to reopen in spring 2027 or later.

blocks.title: On foot across the Uji Bridge

transit.label: On foot — Byōdō-in → Ujigami-jinja
transit.detail: 20–30 min on foot. Cross the Uji Bridge, then walk along the river past Tō-no-Shima (塔の島), the island in the river, to the east bank. The Uji Bridge is one of the three oldest bridges in Japan.

items.detail: Shrine on the east bank of the river, across from Byōdō-in. The grounds are small: about 20 min is enough. Entry is free. 💴 Anything you buy at the shrine (charms, fortunes) is cash only. Last entry 16:10; the shrine closes at 16:20.
items.about: Uji's second World Heritage site, after Byōdō-in. The honden (main sanctuary) is a National Treasure and the oldest surviving shrine building in Japan. It is three Heian-period sanctuaries under one roof: the outer two large, the middle one small. The haiden (worship hall), also a National Treasure, is a residential-style building. It is said to be a surviving part of the Uji detached palace.

blocks.title: Lunch, then the train one stop to Ōbaku

transit.label: JR Nara line — Uji → Ōbaku
transit.detail: Walk back over the Uji Bridge and have lunch on the street leading up to Byōdō-in. Uji is known for matcha (green tea). Allow time for a proper sit-down meal. Then walk to JR Uji station and ride one stop north to Ōbaku: about 15 min from the shrine, not counting lunch. This ride is already included in the fare shown on the morning train to Uji.

items.detail: Chinese-style Zen temple, 5 min on foot from Ōbaku station. Allow 30 min–1 hour. Reception closes at 16:30.
items.about: Manpuku-ji was founded in 1661 by Ingen Ryūki, a Chinese monk from Fujian. He came to Japan at 63 with twenty disciples, and named the temple after his own temple in China. It was built in the Chinese style of the late Ming dynasty and still looks it. The halls stand in one straight line, with matching buildings mirrored left and right. Look for swastika-pattern railings, round windows, peach-shaped carvings on the doors and the arched ceiling known as the Ōbaku ceiling. The paths are paved with square stones set as diamonds, to look like a dragon's scales. Three halls are National Treasures. One of them is the main hall, which the temple says is the only historic building in Japan made of teak. The sutras are still chanted with a Chinese reading.

transit.label: JR Nara line — Ōbaku → Kyoto
transit.detail: About 20 min, three trains an hour. Ōbaku station has no ticket office, and staff are there only at some times of day. The ticket gates take IC cards. This ride is already included in the fare shown on the morning train to Uji.

notes_top: 💴 Going inside the Phoenix Hall costs ¥300 on top of the Byōdō-in entry ticket. You pay at the desk inside the garden on the day. Have coins ready.

backup.title: If it rains: most of this day is indoors
backup.detail: The Byōdō-in museum, the inside of the Phoenix Hall and Manpuku-ji's halls are all indoors. The only parts outdoors are the walks over the Uji Bridge: from Byōdō-in to Ujigami-jinja (20–30 min), and back to JR Uji station. In rain, walk them quickly and spend longer in the Byōdō-in museum instead. Little of this day is lost to rain. That makes it the best day to swap with Sunday Nov 1 (Kurama to Kibune) or Tuesday Nov 3 (Takao and Jingo-ji) if either of those turns out wet.

title: Hiroshima — the Peace Park (and the move)

items.detail: Leave at 09:30 for the 10:02 Shinkansen. The Shinkansen gate is about 10 min from the hotel door. The train time decides when you leave, so you don't need to know the check-out time. Nothing to pay here: the ten nights and the Kyoto city lodging tax were paid at this desk when you arrived.

transit.label: Walk — the Dormy Inn to Kyoto Station
transit.detail: 3 min from the hotel to the Central (Karasuma) gate on the north side of Kyoto Station. Then walk through the station to the Shinkansen transfer gate: about 10 min in all from the hotel door. You are through the gate by about 09:40, on the platform 20 min before the train.

transit.label: Nozomi 13 — Kyoto 10:02 → Hiroshima 11:38
transit.detail: 1 hour 36 min, no change, on the Tōkaidō–Sanyō Shinkansen. If you miss it: the same ticket is valid in the non-reserved cars of a later train. The 10:25, 10:46 and 11:02 all still keep the afternoon plan. The 11:25 is the latest train that still keeps the plan. The 12:02 is too late: you would reach the Peace Memorial Museum after its last walk-up entry. Any seat is fine. There is no view of Mount Fuji on this line, so it doesn't matter which side you sit.
transit.cost_note: reserved paper ticket, bought from a machine or the ticket office at Kyoto Station on Oct 28

transit.label: Walk — Hiroshima Station to the Sotetsu Fresa Inn
transit.detail: About 300 m, 4 min, on the south side of the station.

blocks.title: Leave the bags at the hotel at about 11:50 (check-in from 15:00)

items.detail: Put both bags in the self-service cloakroom on the 2nd floor. It is free for guests, on the day they check in and the day they check out, so it covers today and the day you leave Hiroshima. Staff don't take the bags. You lock them yourself with a wire lock that opens with a transit IC card (such as Suica). If you don't have one, the hotel lends you a card. If the cloakroom is full or the card won't read: use the coin lockers at Hiroshima Station, 4 min back. That costs only a locker fee and a few minutes. Check-in is from 15:00 and the front desk is open until midnight, so you can check in after the museum. You pay at this hotel: ¥40,201 for the two nights, plus ¥400 Hiroshima prefectural lodging tax.

transit.label: Walk — Hiroshima Station to Shukkei-en
transit.detail: 10 min on foot, after lunch near the station (okonomiyaki, Hiroshima's own dish). If it rains: take the Hiroden tram to Shukkeien-mae, then walk 2 min. The fare is ¥240. Get on and off by any door, and tap your card when you get on and when you get off. The plan is to walk, so the day's total cost does not include this fare.

items.detail: Allow 45 min–1 hour to walk round the garden. ⚠ Last entry 16:30; the garden closes at 17:00.
items.about: A stroll garden (a garden made to be walked round) laid out in 1620 for Asano Nagaakira, the first Asano lord of Hiroshima. It is also an A-bomb site. It is 1.3 km from the hypocentre, the point the bomb exploded above. After the bombing it was used as a relief station and as a mass burial ground. Trees that survived the bomb still stand in it.

transit.label: Hiroden tram — Shukkei-en → the Peace Park
transit.detail: Line 9 from Shukkeien-mae. Change at Hatchōbori to line 2 or line 6. About 20 min in all.
transit.payment: Get on and off by any door: since July 2026 a single adult may use any door. Tap the card reader when you get on, and again when you get off. Hold the card on the reader until it shows ありがとうございました ("thank you"). You tap twice even though every trip costs the same ¥240. If your card balance is too low, pay the full ¥240 in cash or with another card.
transit.cost_note: the same fare on every Hiroden line

items.detail: Allow 35–40 min on foot. Free, open at all hours. It is busier on a Saturday. The main stops: the Cenotaph, the Children's Peace Monument, the Korean A-bomb Victims Memorial and the Peace Bell.
items.about: The architect Tange Kenzō laid out the park on one line. From the Cenotaph, its arch frames the Flame of Peace and the A-bomb Dome behind it. The Children's Peace Monument is for Sasaki Sadako and the other children killed by the bomb. Sadako's story is linked to folded paper cranes, and a bronze girl on top of the monument holds up a golden crane.

items.detail: 5 min walk further, at the north end of the park. Allow 20–25 min to walk all round the ruin and along the riverbank path up to it. You see it from outside only. As a preserved ruin, it has never been open to visitors. No scaffolding or works are due during your visit: the city's new 13-year preservation programme runs its tests on samples away from the building.
items.about: The building was the Hiroshima Prefectural Products Exhibition Hall, designed by the Czech architect Jan Letzel and finished in 1915. It stood about 160 m from the hypocentre and everyone inside was killed.

items.detail: 5 min walk back into the park, then allow 25–30 min.
items.about: A round hall of remembrance, sunk below ground level, shows a 360-degree panorama of the destroyed city. It is made from about 140,000 tiles, one for each person estimated to have died by the end of 1945. The register of victims and the library of survivors' accounts are the part visitors find most moving.

blocks.title: The Peace Memorial Museum (last stop of the day)

items.detail: Last stop of the day, with nothing after it. Allow 1 hour 45 min–2 hours. ⚠ The 17:30 on this card is the last time you can buy a ticket at the door. From 17:30 to 18:30 you can only enter with an online timed ticket, and none is booked. The museum is open until 19:00, with last entry 18:30. Even if the day runs very late, you arrive by about 16:15. That is 1 hour 15 min before 17:30, with time for the whole visit before the 19:00 close. Take it slower if you want to.
items.about: The route runs from the introduction to the reality of the bombing, the danger of nuclear weapons, and Hiroshima's history since 1945. The Main Building, designed by Tange Kenzō in 1955, holds the victims' belongings and their testimony.

transit.label: Hiroden tram — the Peace Park → Hiroshima Station
transit.detail: Lines 2 and 6 from Genbaku Dōme-mae (原爆ドーム前) run to Hiroshima Station, the end of the line: 17–20 min. Dinner and the hotel are both at the station. Leave the museum at 18:00–18:15 to sit down to dinner at about 18:45–19:00.
transit.payment: The same as the tram from Shukkei-en. Get on and off by any door. Tap the card when you get on, and again when you get off. Hold the card on the reader until it shows ありがとうございました ("thank you"). Two taps for the flat ¥240 fare. If your card balance is too low, pay the full ¥240 in cash or with another card.
transit.cost_note: the same fare on every Hiroden line

notes_top: 💴 Icchan takes cash only. Masaru takes cash or QR payment (PayPay), but no cards. The Peace Memorial Museum (¥200) and Shukkei-en (¥350) are paid at the gate. If you are short of cash, use an ATM at Hiroshima Station when you arrive.
notes: 🍳 At check-in, ask what time breakfast starts. If it starts by 06:30, eat breakfast at the hotel tomorrow and take the 06:58 JR Sanyō line train to Miyajimaguchi. If it starts later, buy breakfast at a konbini and take the 06:40 train instead.

backup.title: If it rains: the Prefectural Art Museum instead of Shukkei-en
backup.detail: The Hiroshima Prefectural Art Museum is next door to Shukkei-en and uses the same tram stop. Open Saturday 09:00–17:00, last entry 16:30, ¥510. Shukkei-en is the only part of the day exposed to rain. Everything else is indoors, apart from the Peace Park itself. You lose something by swapping: the garden is an A-bomb site as well as a garden, and the art museum does not replace that. There are only two days in Hiroshima, so there is no other day to move the garden to. ⚑ Make the same swap if you are too tired for the garden. The day has time for either.

title: Miyajima & the ascent of Misen

blocks.title: Early train and ferry to Miyajima

transit.label: JR Sanyō line — Hiroshima → Miyajimaguchi
transit.detail: 26 min on the Sanyō line, all stations. Trains leave Hiroshima at 06:25, 06:40 and 06:58. The station is 4 min from the hotel. Take the 06:40 and eat a konbini breakfast. If the hotel breakfast is already being served when you come down, eat quickly and take the 06:58. That costs about 20 min, which the day can spare. Start early: the shrine opens at 06:30, and you must be off the mountain in daylight.
transit.cost_note: one way; ¥840 round trip

transit.label: JR ferry — Miyajimaguchi → Miyajima
transit.detail: 10 min, about 4 sailings an hour. Sailings between 09:10 and 16:10 go past the great torii when the tide allows.
transit.payment: No ticket to buy. Tap your IC card once at the gate inside the Miyajimaguchi terminal, before you walk down to the boat. That one tap pays the ¥200 fare and the ¥100 island tax. There is nothing to do on the boat.
transit.cost_note: ¥200 fare + ¥100 Miyajima visitor tax, charged on the outbound crossing only; one IC tap at the gate pays both

items.detail: 12–15 min walk along the shore from the pier. Allow 40–45 min inside. The route through the shrine is one-way. The combined ticket adds the Treasure Hall: buy it only if you want to see it. ⚠ The East Corridor, where the one-way route starts, is being strengthened until December 2026. The shrine has announced no closure or detour for it.
items.about: Corridors on pillars over the water link the main halls, the Marōdo shrine, the hirabutai platform and the Noh stage of 1680. The Noh stage is built out over the sea. A Noh stage normally has a jar buried under its floor to make the dancers’ steps ring. This one stands over the sea, so it cannot have one. Its floor is built to carry the sound instead. The shrine was founded in 593, and Taira no Kiyomori built the complex over the water in about 1168.

items.detail: 8 min uphill from the shrine. Allow about 25 min. ⚠ It closes at 16:30, an hour before the shrine. The five-storey pagoda next to it is wrapped in scaffolding for repair until 20 November 2027, so you will not see it.
items.about: Toyotomi Hideyoshi ordered this sutra hall in 1587. Its floor covers 857 tatami mats. It is called Senjōkaku, ‘hall of a thousand mats’. Hideyoshi died before it was finished, so it has no ceiling and no front wall. You walk into a building that was never completed.

blocks.title: Daishō-in temple and the start of the trail

items.detail: 15 min through the lanes from Senjōkaku. Allow 45 min–1 hour. Free. The Misen trail starts here, so this is your last stop before the climb. ⏱ Start up the trail by 10:15, even if you have not finished at Daishō-in. That leaves 2½ hours for the climb and 45 min on top before 13:30, the latest you can leave the summit for the ropeway booking.
items.about: Daishō-in is a head temple of the Omuro school of Shingon Buddhism. Look for the Henjōkutsu cave, lined with the 88 icons of the Shikoku pilgrimage, the sutra wheels set into the stair handrail, and the rows of rakan (Buddhist saint) statues.

blocks.title: Up Misen by the Daishō-in trail (大聖院コース)

maps.label: Misen trail map — Miyajima Tourist Association
maps.note: All three official routes up Misen, including the Daishō-in course we climb and the Momijidani course we come down.

maps.label: AllTrails — Daishō-in course
maps.note: The ascent we are doing: stone staircase most of the way, through the Jizō statues.

transit.label: On foot — Daishō-in → the summit of Misen
transit.detail: ⏱ Start up by 10:15. Plan on 2–2½ hours up. The trail is 2.6 km long and climbs from sea level to 535 m, on stone steps almost all the way. Stone markers (chō stones, 24 in all) count off the distance. Near the bottom the trail enters the primeval forest that is part of the World Heritage site. Up and down on foot takes 3–5 hours in all. ⚠ This is the hardest climb of the trip. It is harder than the Momijidani trail (your way down) and steeper underfoot than Mt Takao (day 5). 🔴 Nothing is sold on the mountain: carry food and water.

items.detail: Allow 45 min–1 hour on the top: Misen Hondō hall, the Kuguri-iwa rock arch, and the observation deck at 535 m. The deck is open 10:00–16:00, and you reach it hours before it closes. ⚠ Reikadō hall burned down in May 2026 and there is no date for rebuilding: assume it is gone.
items.about: From the deck you look out over the islands of the Seto Inland Sea (Setouchi). The deck was rebuilt in 2013 to a design by Hiroshi Sambuichi, made for sitting and looking at the view. The flame that burned in Reikadō survived the fire and is now kept as several divided flames. The primeval forest on Misen is a National Natural Monument.

blocks.title: Down by the Momijidani trail (紅葉谷コース)

transit.label: On foot — down to Momijidani and the town
transit.detail: Allow 1¼–1½ hours down. This is the easier of the two trails. It is still stone steps and tree roots all the way, so it takes well over half the time of the climb. It ends at Momijidani Park, 15 min from Omotesandō, the shopping street with the late lunch: anago-meshi (conger eel on rice), and momiji-manjū (maple-leaf cakes) hot off the griddle. The ferry pier is at the far end of the same street. ⏱ Leave the summit by 14:15. You then reach Omotesandō by about 16:00, in time for Hayashi’s 16:30 last order. If you leave later, eat at Ueno on the mainland instead (last order 18:30). Do not start down after 15:30: you need to be off the mountain before sunset at 17:12. If the climb has run late: go down the way you came up, by the Daishō-in trail. The temple says that trail stays light longer, and Momijidani is a valley that gets dark early. If your legs are finished at the top: take the ropeway down. 8 November is a reservation-only day on the ropeway, and you have a booking: 14:00–14:15, one person (number and QR code in the booking e-mail and the guide's bookings appendix). 🔴 Be at the upper ropeway station (Shishiiwa) between 14:00 and 14:15: the booking lapses once that time has passed. Shishiiwa is about 30 min on foot from the summit, so leave the summit by 13:30. Show the booking QR code at the platform. It is in the confirmation email and in the bookings appendix at the back of the guide PDF. ⚠ Even with a booking you may wait for a car: November is the ropeway’s busiest month. The last car down is at 16:30. If the queue is too long, the only other way down is on foot, and you do not want to start that walk at dusk.

blocks.title: Back lane and shore walk at dusk

items.label: Machiya-dōri back lane, then the great torii at dusk
items.detail: About 45 min. Walk Machiya-dōri, the back lane behind the shopping street, then the shore. Nothing on this walk has a closing time, so if anything earlier ran late, cut this short. Today’s closing times: summit deck 16:00, Senjōkaku 16:30, Daishō-in 17:00, shrine 17:30. Sunset is 17:12 and it stays light enough to walk until about 17:38. You come down off the mountain at about 14:45–15:15, so there is no hurry.

transit.label: JR ferry — Miyajima 17:25 → Miyajimaguchi
transit.detail: 10 min. Later ferries: 17:40, 17:55, 18:10, 18:25, 18:40, 19:00, 19:30, 20:00, 20:42, 21:25, and the last at 22:14. A second company runs the same crossing with its own boats.
transit.payment: Tap your IC card at the gate on the Miyajima pier before boarding, as this morning. It takes ¥200: the island tax is charged only on the way out.
transit.cost_note: fare only; the ¥100 visitor tax was paid on the way out

transit.label: JR Sanyō line — Miyajimaguchi 17:49 → Hiroshima 18:20
transit.detail: 31 min on the same all-stations line, 5 min longer than the morning’s 26 min: evening trains have more slack in the timetable. Later trains: 18:03, 18:19, 18:31, then every 15–20 min until the last at 23:27. If JR is not running: the Hiroden tram from Hiroden-Miyajimaguchi also goes into the city. After the hardest day of the trip you may come back on a later boat or train. Masaru, tonight’s dinner, takes orders until 22:00.
transit.cost_note: one way; ¥840 round trip

notes_top: 💴 Carry cash for the shrine entry and, if you use it, the ropeway (¥1,100 one way down). The ropeway booking holds a place; it is not a ticket. Hayashi, the lunch restaurant, takes cards and QR payment. Momijidō’s maple-leaf cakes are cash only. The ferry needs no cash: one IC tap at the gate pays it.

backup.title: If it rains: skip the mountain, keep the shrine and temples
backup.detail: Skip the climb. Keep Itsukushima Shrine, Senjōkaku and Daishō-in, add the Treasure Hall, and add the Miyajima Public Aquarium (¥1,420, 09:00–17:00, last entry 16:00). That fills about 5 hours, half a day. A second indoor option is the Miyajima History and Folklore Museum. It is closed on Mondays, and today is a Sunday. ⚠ This is a big loss: the climb through the primeval forest and the summit are the reason for the day.

blocks.title: Check out by 11:00, then a free morning

items.detail: Breakfast, then leave the room by 11:00. You can leave your bags in the self-service cloakroom on the 2nd floor on check-out day too. Lock them with your IC card, the same way as when you arrived. If the cloakroom is full or the card won't read: use the coin lockers at Hiroshima Station. You are free until about 12:15. Then collect your bags and walk to the station to buy lunch before the 12:43 train. Nothing is planned this morning: spend it however you like.

transit.label: Walk — the hotel to Hiroshima Station
transit.detail: 300 m, 4 min.

blocks.title: Ekiben (boxed lunch): buy it before the Shinkansen gates

items.detail: Yume Hyakusen (夢百選), a bento and souvenir counter on the 2nd floor of the ekie building at Hiroshima Station. It is outside the ticket gates, on the concourse between the hotel side of the station and the Shinkansen gates. 🔴 Buy your box before you go through the Shinkansen gates: once you are inside, you can't come back to it. Buy any time between about 11:30 and 12:30, so you don't need to hurry. Look for the anago-meshi bentō (conger eel on rice) from Ueno, a shop in Miyajimaguchi. It has been sold since 1901 and is named after Miyajima, the island you visited yesterday. ⚠ The box is delivered from Miyajimaguchi and can sell out. If it has: there are six ekiben counters inside the Shinkansen gates. Five are open on Mondays, and two of those are on the Tokyo-direction platform. The one that closes on Mondays is Musashi (むさし), the best-known bento kitchen in the station.

transit.label: Nozomi 26 — Hiroshima 12:43 → Tokyo 16:33
transit.detail: 3 hours 50 min. Your seat is E, on the Mount Fuji side going east. Fuji is visible at about 15:35–15:55. If you miss the train: the same ticket is valid in the non-reserved cars of any of the next six trains, at 13:03, 13:12, 13:18, 13:43, 14:03 and 14:14. The hotel desk closes at 22:00. On the 12:43 you reach the hotel about 5 hours before that.
transit.cost_note: reserved paper ticket, bought from a machine or the ticket office at Kyoto Station on Oct 28

transit.label: JR — Tokyo → Akihabara
transit.detail: 2 stops, about 4 min, on the Yamanote or the Keihin-Tōhoku line, whichever comes first. With bags, allow 20–25 min from the Shinkansen platform to the hotel door.
transit.cost_note: with Suica; ¥160 with a paper ticket

transit.label: Walk — Akihabara Station to the hotel

items.detail: The same hotel as your first Tokyo stay, booked separately. Check-in is 14:00–22:00. 🔴 22:00 is a strict deadline: the desk does not check anyone in after it. Arriving at about 16:55 gives you about 5 hours to spare. The booking can't be moved to another date. Nothing was prepaid. At the front desk you pay ¥48,360 for the two nights plus about ¥400 Tokyo lodging tax. Nothing is planned after dinner tonight.

transit.label: JR Chūō-Sōbu — Akihabara → Koishikawa-Kōrakuen
transit.detail: Chūō-Sōbu line to Iidabashi, then walk to the garden gate. The garden opens at 09:00, so start the day there.
transit.cost_note: both JR rides to Ryōgoku together: Akihabara to Iidabashi ¥155, then Iidabashi to Ryōgoku ¥199; Suica fares

items.detail: Allow 1–1½ hours. Go in the morning. Last entry 16:30.
items.about: Tokyo's oldest surviving Edo-period daimyō (feudal lord's) garden, begun in 1629 by the Mito branch of the Tokugawa family. It is both a Special Place of Scenic Beauty and a Special Historic Site, which is rare. The garden puts Japanese and Chinese scenes side by side: the Engetsu-kyō full-moon bridge, the Tsūten-kyō bridge, a miniature version of the Ōi river (Ōi-gawa) and a rice field.

transit.label: JR Chūō-Sōbu — Iidabashi → Ryōgoku
transit.detail: Walk back to Iidabashi station, then take the Chūō-Sōbu line east to Ryōgoku: about 15 min. This fare is already counted on the ride out this morning. Lunch is chanko-nabe, the sumo wrestlers' stew and Ryōgoku's local dish. The Edo-Tokyo Museum is a few minutes' walk from the station.

items.detail: Allow 2½–3 hours: you will need all of it. Last admission is 30 min before closing (17:00 on a Tuesday). No booking needed: buy a ticket at the door on the day.
items.about: The museum reopened on 31 March 2026 after a four-year renewal, rebuilt as an immersive museum. You can walk into the Nakamura-za playhouse and, since the renewal, into a tenement room. There is a 26 m span of the Nihonbashi bridge and the full-size Hattori clock tower from 1890s Ginza. Galleries with projected images follow the city as Edo becomes Tokyo.

blocks.title: Optional: on to Kiyosumi garden, 2 stops east

transit.label: Toei Ōedo — Ryōgoku → Kiyosumi-teien
transit.detail: Walk 3 min from JR Ryōgoku station to the Toei Ōedo line station. Take the Ōedo line 2 stops to Kiyosumi-shirakawa: about 10 min including the walk. Then walk to the garden. 🔴 Get there before 16:30, the garden's last entry.
transit.cost_note: for the whole detour: ¥178 on the Ōedo line out, ¥178 back, and ¥155 on JR from Ryōgoku home. If you skip Kiyosumi, you pay only the ¥155 JR fare

items.detail: Optional: decide on the day. Allow 40 min–1 hour. The day works without it. 🔴 Go only if there is time: last entry is 16:30 and the gate shuts at 17:00. To have 40 min in the garden, walk in by about 16:15. If you leave the museum later than about 16:00, skip the garden.
items.about: A stroll garden (a garden made to be walked round) laid out around the Daisensui pond. Famous named stones are set along the path, and the Ryōtei pavilion stands out over the water.

transit.label: Ōedo then JR Chūō-Sōbu — Kiyosumi-shirakawa → Akihabara, changing at Ryōgoku
transit.detail: The same way back: the Ōedo line 2 stops to Ryōgoku, then the Chūō-Sōbu line 2 stops to Akihabara. 20–30 min including the walk out of the garden. The fare is counted on the ride out to Kiyosumi. If you skip Kiyosumi, you are already at Ryōgoku: take the Chūō-Sōbu line straight home. You pay only the ¥155 JR fare and none of the Ōedo fares.

blocks.title: Errands today: the hotel bill, and tomorrow's Skyliner seat if you haven't bought it

items.label: Tomorrow's Skyliner seat (only if you didn't buy it at Narita)
items.detail: If you already have the Nov 11 ticket, skip this. Otherwise buy it today, while you are in town: the 11:05 from Nippori to Narita Terminal 1. Buy it at the Keisei ticket machine or counter at Keisei Ueno or Nippori station. If you wait until tomorrow morning, the 11:05 may be full.

items.label: Pay the hotel bill tonight
items.detail: At the front desk: ¥48,360 for the two nights plus about ¥400 lodging tax. Pay tonight, because tomorrow you leave at 10:30 for the Skyliner.

backup.title: If it rains: no change
backup.detail: The Edo-Tokyo Museum, 2½–3 hours of the day, is indoors. Only the two gardens are outdoors, and both are fine to walk in light rain. No rain plan is needed.

items.detail: Check-out is 11:00, but leave at about 10:30. Breakfast starts early enough to eat before you leave. 🔴 You pay ¥48,360 for the two nights at this desk. If you did not pay last night, be at the desk by 10:15. Leaving 30 min before check-out costs you nothing. It is your only spare time before the airport. You may need it if the tax-refund check at customs is slow, and the ticket does not say when El Al's check-in closes.

transit.label: JR — Akihabara → Nippori
transit.detail: 4 stops. At Nippori, follow the Keisei signs to the Skyliner platform: allow about 7 min.
transit.cost_note: with Suica; ¥200 with a paper ticket

transit.label: Skyliner — Nippori → Narita T1
transit.detail: Take Skyliner No. 33 at 11:05. It reaches Terminal 1 at 11:43, four hours before LY92 leaves. If you miss it: the 11:25 and the 11:40 both still get you to Terminal 1 more than three hours before the flight. The last Skyliner from Nippori is at 20:25. You should already have the ticket: you bought it at Narita on arrival or on Nov 10.
transit.cost_note: station ticket, one way; some published fares say ¥2,470

items.detail: Leaving the hotel at about 10:30 gets you to Terminal 1 at 11:43, four hours before the flight. Aim to be at the airport by about 12:45. That is 3 h before the flight, the usual time allowed for security. ⚠ The ticket does not give El Al's check-in closing time, so the 12:45 target is based only on that usual 3 h.

items.label: Tax refund at airport customs: only for shopping on or after Nov 1
items.detail: Japan's tax-free shopping rules changed on Nov 1. Both of your shopping days were before that date. The camera, the pen, the watch and the Uniqlo shopping need nothing at the airport. Anything else you bought on or after Nov 1 is different. The tax on it is refunded only after customs confirms the goods are leaving Japan. Customs does this before you go to the El Al counter.
